title.zh: 卷四十六 志第三十六 百官一
title.raw: 卷四十六 志第三十六 百官一 Volume 46 Treatises 41: Official Posts 1

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 唐之官制，其名號祿秩雖因時增損，而大抵皆沿隋故。

translations.literal: As for the Tang official system, although its titles, designations, salaries, and ranks were increased or reduced according to the times, on the whole they all followed the Sui precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang bureaucracy, for all that its titles, grades, salaries, and ranks shifted with the times, largely followed the Sui model.

sentences.zh: 其官司之別，曰省、曰臺、曰寺、曰監、曰衞、曰府，各統其屬，以分職定位。

translations.literal: The divisions of its offices and agencies were called Departments, Bureaus, Directorates, Commissions, Guards, and Offices; each governed its subordinates to assign duties and fix positions.
translations.idiomatic: Government agencies were grouped as Departments, Bureaus, Directorates, Commissions, Guards, and Offices, each commanding its subordinates so that duties and posts were clearly assigned.

sentences.zh: 其辯貴賤、敍勞能，則有品、有爵、有勳、有階，以時考覈而升降之，所以任羣材、治百事。

translations.literal: To distinguish noble from base and to arrange merit and ability, there were ranks, enfeoffments, orders of merit, and grades, which were examined at set times and raised or lowered—by this means all talents were employed and the hundred affairs were governed.
translations.idiomatic: To distinguish status and reward service, the system used official ranks, noble titles, orders of merit, and grade steps, reviewed on schedule for promotion or demotion—thus deploying talent across every branch of administration.

sentences.zh: 其為法則精而密，其施於事則簡而易行，所以然者，由職有常守，而位有常員也。

translations.literal: As law it was refined and close; in application to affairs it was simple and easy to carry out. The reason was that offices had fixed duties and posts had fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations were intricate in design yet straightforward in practice, because every office had a defined charge and every post a fixed complement.

sentences.zh: 方唐之盛時，其制如此。

translations.literal: At the height of Tang prosperity, the system was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the system at the height of Tang power.

sentences.zh: 蓋其始未嘗不欲立制度、明紀綱為萬世法，而常至於交侵紛亂者，由其時君不能慎守，而徇一切之苟且，故其事愈繁而官益冗，至失其職業而卒不能復。

translations.literal: At the outset they had never failed to wish to establish institutions and clarify statutes and regulations as a model for ten thousand generations; yet they often came to mutual encroachment and disorder because the rulers of the time could not guard them carefully and indulged every expedient compromise, so that affairs grew ever more complex and offices ever more redundant, until they lost their proper functions and in the end could not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty had always intended to set institutions and clarify regulations as a lasting model, yet practice often dissolved into overlapping jurisdictions and confusion, because successive emperors failed to uphold the system and settled for makeshift compromises. Affairs multiplied, posts proliferated, offices lost their proper functions, and the original order could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗省內外官，定制為七百三十員，曰：「吾以此待天下賢材，足矣。」

translations.literal: At first, Taizong reduced the inner and outer officials and fixed the quota at seven hundred thirty posts, saying: "With this I shall await the worthy talent of the realm—enough."
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign, Emperor Taizong cut the inner and outer bureaucracy to a fixed quota of seven hundred thirty posts, declaring, "This is ample to employ the worthy talent of the empire."

sentences.zh: 然是時已有員外置，其後又有特置，同正員。

translations.literal: Yet even then there were already supernumerary appointments; later there were also specially created posts, equal to regular incumbents.
translations.idiomatic: Even then, however, supernumerary appointees already existed; later came specially created posts treated as the equal of regular incumbents.

sentences.zh: 至於檢校、兼、守、判、知之類，皆非本制。

translations.literal: As for acting, concurrent, provisional, acting-in-charge, and supervisory categories, none were part of the original system.
translations.idiomatic: Titles such as acting commissioner, concurrent appointment, provisional holder, acting judge, and supervisory assignment lay outside the original design.

sentences.zh: 又有置使之名，或因事而置，事已則罷，或遂置而不廢。

translations.literal: There were also titles of specially appointed commissioners: some were created for a particular affair and abolished when the affair ended; others were created and then never abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Special commissioners were appointed as needed—some dissolved when the task ended, others became permanent fixtures.

sentences.zh: 其名類繁多，莫能徧舉。

translations.literal: Their names and categories were numerous beyond full enumeration.
translations.idiomatic: The varieties multiplied beyond exhaustive listing.

sentences.zh: 自中世已後，盜起兵興，又有軍功之官，遂不勝其濫矣。

translations.literal: From the mid-dynasty onward, bandits rose and armies were raised; there were also offices for military merit, and the abuse could no longer be borne.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-Tang period, rebellion and civil war brought a flood of military-merit appointments until the system could no longer contain the excess.

sentences.zh: 故採其綱目條理可為後法，及事雖非正後世遵用因仍而不能改者，著於篇。

translations.literal: Therefore we have gathered those outlines and arrangements that may serve as models for later ages, and those matters that, though not orthodox, later generations followed in succession and could not change—set down in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter therefore records the main outlines that may serve as precedent, together with irregular practices that later ages adopted and could not undo.

sentences.zh: 宰相之職宰相之職，佐天子總百官、治萬事，其任重矣。

translations.literal: The office of Chancellor—the office of Chancellor assists the Son of Heaven in overseeing the hundred officials and governing the ten thousand affairs; its burden is heavy indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellorship. The chancellor assists the emperor in directing all officials and governing every branch of state affairs—a burden of the greatest weight.

sentences.zh: 然自漢以來，位號不同，而唐世宰相，名尤不正。

translations.literal: Yet from Han onward the titles and designations differed, and under Tang the name of chancellor was especially irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times the title had varied, but under Tang the designation of chancellor was more irregular than ever.

sentences.zh: 初，唐因隋制，以三省之長中書令、侍中、尚書令共議國政，此宰相職也。

translations.literal: At first Tang followed the Sui system: the heads of the Three Departments—Director of the Secretariat, Head of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs—jointly deliberated on state policy; this was the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Tang followed Sui practice: the heads of the Secretariat, the Chancellery, and the Department of State Affairs deliberated together on national policy—the core chancellor posts.

sentences.zh: 其後，以太宗嘗為尚書令，臣下避不敢居其職，由是僕射為尚書省長官，與侍中、中書令號為宰相，其品位既崇，不欲輕以授人，故常以他官居宰相職，而假以他名。

translations.literal: Later, because Taizong had once been Director of the Department of State Affairs, ministers shrank from holding that post; hence the Vice Directors became heads of the Department and, with the Head of the Chancellery and Director of the Secretariat, were styled chancellors. Their rank being already exalted, the court did not wish to grant the title lightly; therefore other officials often held chancellor duties under borrowed designations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Taizong had once served as Director of the Department of State Affairs, later appointees declined that post, and the Vice Directors became the department heads who, with the Head of the Chancellery and the Director of the Secretariat, were called chancellors. The rank was so exalted that the court hesitated to confer it openly; chancellor duties were therefore often performed by other officials under alternate titles.

sentences.zh: 自太宗時，杜淹以吏部尚書參議朝政，魏徵以祕書監參預朝政，其後或曰「參議得失」、「參知政事」之類，其名非一，皆宰相職也。

translations.literal: From Taizong's time, Du Yan as Minister of Personnel deliberated on court policy; Wei Zheng as Director of the Palace Library participated in court policy. Later there were such titles as "Deliberating on Right and Wrong" and "Participating in State Affairs"—the names were not one, but all were chancellor offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, Du Yan joined policy deliberation as Minister of Personnel and Wei Zheng as Director of the Palace Library. Later titles such as "Deliberating on Policy" and "Participating in Government" proliferated—all equivalent to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，僕射李靖以疾辭位，詔疾小瘳，三兩日一至中書門下平章事，而「平章事」之名蓋起於此。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, Vice Director Li Jing resigned his post on grounds of illness. An edict said that when his illness was slightly improved he should come once every two or three days to the Secretariat-Chancellery as Associate Director of the Department; the name "Associate Director" probably arose here.
translations.idiomatic: In 634, Vice Director Li Jing resigned on grounds of illness. The court ordered that once he had recovered slightly he should attend the Secretariat-Chancellery every few days as Associate Director of the Department—the title "pingzhangshi" (Associate Director) appears to date from this episode.

sentences.zh: 其後，李勣以太子詹事同中書門下三品，謂同侍中、中書令也，而「同三品」之名蓋起於此。

translations.literal: Later, Li Ji as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent was made Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery Third Rank, meaning equal to Head of the Chancellery and Director of the Secretariat; the name "Associate Third Rank" probably arose here.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Ji, as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery Third Rank—equal in standing to the Head of the Chancellery and the Director of the Secretariat—giving rise to the title "Associate Third Rank."

sentences.zh: 然二名不專用，而佗官居職者猶假佗名如故。

translations.literal: Yet the two titles were not used exclusively; other officials holding the duties still borrowed other names as before.
translations.idiomatic: Neither title became exclusive; officials performing chancellor duties continued to use other designations as well.

sentences.zh: 自高宗已後，為宰相者必加「同中書門下三品」，雖品高者亦然；

translations.literal: From Gaozong onward, anyone made chancellor had to receive the added title "Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery Third Rank," even those of high rank;
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Gaozong onward, every appointee to the chancellorship received the added title Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery Third Rank, even those already of high rank;

sentences.zh: 惟三公、三師、中書令則否。

translations.literal: only the Three Dukes, Three Preceptors, and Director of the Secretariat did not.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Dukes, the Three Preceptors, and the Director of the Secretariat excepted.

sentences.zh: 其後改易官名，而張文瓘以東臺侍郎同東西臺三品，「同三品」入銜，自文瓘始。

translations.literal: Later official titles were changed, and Zhang Wenguan as Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace was made Associate of the Eastern and Western Terraces Third Rank; "Associate Third Rank" entered the formal title, beginning with Wenguan.
translations.idiomatic: After a further renaming of offices, Zhang Wenguan received the title Associate of the Eastern and Western Terraces Third Rank—the first time "Associate Third Rank" appeared in the formal title.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，以黃門侍郎郭待舉、兵部侍郎岑長倩等同中書門下平章事，「平章事」入銜，自待舉等始。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Guo Daiju as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Cen Changqian as Vice Minister of War were made Associates of the Secretariat-Chancellery as Associate Directors; "Associate Director" entered the formal title, beginning with Daiju and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In 682, Guo Daiju and Cen Changqian were made Associates of the Secretariat-Chancellery as Associate Directors—the first time "pingzhangshi" entered the formal title.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，終唐之世不能改。

translations.literal: From this time onward, through the end of Tang it could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the end of the dynasty, the practice did not change.

sentences.zh: 初，三省長官議事于門下省之政事堂，其後，裴炎自侍中遷中書令，乃徙政事堂於中書省。

translations.literal: At first the heads of the Three Departments deliberated in the Hall of Administration of the Chancellery; later Pei Yan moved from Head of the Chancellery to Director of the Secretariat, and the Hall of Administration was moved to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the three department heads met in the Chancellery's Hall of Administration; when Pei Yan moved from Head of the Chancellery to Director of the Secretariat, the hall was relocated to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元中，張說為相，又改政事堂號「中書門下」，列五房于其後：一曰吏房，二曰樞機房，三曰兵房，四曰戶房，五曰刑禮房，分曹以主眾務焉。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Zhang Yue as chancellor again changed the Hall of Administration to "Secretariat-Chancellery" and set up five chambers behind it: first the Personnel Chamber, second the Secretariat Chamber, third the Military Chamber, fourth the Revenue Chamber, and fifth the Punishments and Rites Chamber, dividing bureaus to oversee the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong, Chancellor Zhang Yue renamed the hall the Secretariat-Chancellery and established five chambers behind it—Personnel, Secretariat, Military, Revenue, and Punishments and Rites—to divide responsibility for the full range of government business.

sentences.zh: 宰相事無不統，故不以一職名官，自開元以後，常以領他職，實欲重其事，而反輕宰相之體。

translations.literal: The chancellor's affairs embraced all without exception, so he was not named by a single office; from Kaiyuan onward he was often made to head other duties as well—intending to magnify the matter, yet in fact diminishing the stature of the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Because the chancellor's authority was all-encompassing, no single title sufficed; from the Kaiyuan period onward chancellors were routinely given additional posts—intended to enhance their weight, but in practice diminishing the dignity of the office.

sentences.zh: 故時方用兵，則為節度使；

translations.literal: Thus when troops were being deployed, he would be made military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: When war was in progress, he might also serve as military commissioner;

sentences.zh: 時崇儒學，則為大學士；

translations.literal: when Confucian learning was honored, he would be made Grand Academician;
translations.idiomatic: when classical learning was in favor, as Grand Academician;

sentences.zh: 時急財用，則為鹽鐵轉運使，又其甚則為延資庫使。

translations.literal: when finances were urgent, he would be made Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner; in the extreme case he would be made Commissioner of the Extended Funds Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: when revenue was pressing, as Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, or in extreme cases as Commissioner of the Extended Funds Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 至於國史、太清宮之類，其名頗多，皆不足取法，故不著其詳。

translations.literal: As for National History, the Great Pure Palace, and the like, their names were quite numerous; none are fit to be taken as models, so their details are not set down.
translations.idiomatic: Titles connected with the National History, the Great Pure Palace, and similar posts were numerous but offer no useful precedent and are therefore omitted here.

sentences.zh: 學士之職學士之職，本以文學言語被顧問，出入侍從，因得參謀議、納諫諍，其禮尤寵；

translations.literal: The office of Academician—the office of Academician was originally for men of literary accomplishment and eloquence to receive consultation, attending in and out as companions, and thereby to participate in counsel, offer remonstrance, and present admonition; the ritual favor was especially great;
translations.idiomatic: The Academicians. The post originally went to men of literary and rhetorical talent who attended the emperor as counselors and companions, joining deliberation and offering remonstrance—an honor of exceptional standing;

sentences.zh: 而翰林院者，待詔之所也。

translations.literal: the Hanlin Academy was the place for awaiting imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: the Hanlin Academy was the court where scholars awaited the emperor's summons.

sentences.zh: 唐制，乘輿所在，必有文詞、經學之士，下至卜、醫、伎術之流，皆直於別院，以備宴見；

translations.literal: Under Tang regulations, wherever the imperial carriage went, there had to be men of literary composition and classical learning, down to diviners, physicians, and practitioners of arts and skills—all stationed in a separate courtyard to be ready for banquet audiences;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, wherever the emperor traveled, literary and classical scholars were on hand, along with diviners, physicians, and skilled artisans, all quartered in a separate compound ready for imperial audiences;

sentences.zh: 而文書詔令，則中書舍人掌之。

translations.literal: documents and edicts were managed by the Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: while formal documents and edicts remained the charge of the Secretariat Drafters.

sentences.zh: 自太宗時，名儒學士時時召以草制，然猶未有名號；

translations.literal: From Taizong's time, eminent Confucian scholars were from time to time summoned to draft edicts, yet there was still no formal designation;
translations.idiomatic: From Taizong's reign eminent scholars were summoned to draft edicts, though no formal title yet existed;

sentences.zh: 乾封以後，始號「北門學士」。

translations.literal: after Qianfeng they were first styled "Northern Gate Academicians."
translations.idiomatic: after the Qianfeng era they were first called Northern Gate Academicians.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初，置「翰林待詔」，以張說、陸堅、張九齡等為之，掌四方表疏批答、應和文章；

translations.literal: Early in Xuanzong's reign, "Hanlin Awaiting Edict" was established; Zhang Yue, Lu Jian, Zhang Jiuling, and others were appointed, charged with drafting replies to memorials from the four quarters and composing matching literary pieces;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign the court created Hanlin Awaiting Edict posts, held by Zhang Yue, Lu Jian, Zhang Jiuling, and others, to draft replies to memorials from the provinces and compose literary pieces for court occasions;

sentences.zh: 既而又以中書務劇，文書多壅滯，乃選文學之士，號「翰林供奉」，與集賢院學士分掌制詔書敕。

translations.literal: Then, because Secretariat business was heavy and documents were often blocked and delayed, literary scholars were selected and styled "Hanlin Attendants," sharing with the Academicians of the Hall of Assembled Worthies the drafting of edicts and imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Secretariat business grew overwhelming and documents piled up, literary scholars were selected as Hanlin Attendants to share edict drafting with the Academicians of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 開元二十六年，又改翰林供奉為學士，別置學士院，專掌內命。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan, Hanlin Attendants were again changed to Academicians; a separate Academy was established, exclusively charged with inner commands.
translations.idiomatic: In 738 the Hanlin Attendants were renamed Academicians, a separate Hanlin Academy was established, and it took exclusive charge of confidential imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 凡拜免將相、號令征伐，皆用白麻。

translations.literal: All appointments and dismissals of generals and chancellors, and all orders for campaigns and punitive expeditions, used white hemp paper.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments and dismissals of generals and ministers, and orders for military campaigns, were issued on white hemp paper.

sentences.zh: 其後，選用益重，而禮遇益親，至號為「內相」，又以為天子私人。

translations.literal: Later their selection grew weightier and their ceremonial treatment more intimate, until they were styled "inner chancellor" and regarded as the Son of Heaven's private men.
translations.idiomatic: Their selection grew more prestigious and their treatment more intimate, until they were called inner chancellors and regarded as the emperor's personal counselors.

sentences.zh: 凡充其職者無定員，自諸曹尚書下至校書郎，皆得與選。

translations.literal: Those who filled the post had no fixed quota; from ministers of the various bureaus down to proofreaders, all could be selected.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed quota; appointees ranged from bureau ministers down to proofreaders.

sentences.zh: 入院一歲，則遷知制誥，未知制誥者不作文書。

translations.literal: After one year in the Academy they were promoted to Drafting Edicts; those not yet Drafting Edicts did not compose documents.
translations.idiomatic: After one year in the Academy they were promoted to Drafting Edicts; only those so promoted could compose official documents.

sentences.zh: 班次各以其官，內宴則居宰相之下，一品之上。

translations.literal: Seating order followed each man's office; at inner banquets they sat below the chancellor and above first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Seating followed regular rank; at inner banquets they sat below the chancellor but above first-rank officials.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，又置「學士承旨」。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time, "Academician Recipient of Edicts" was also established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong the post of Academician Recipient of Edicts was added.

sentences.zh: 唐之學士，弘文、集賢分隸中書、門下省，而翰林學士獨無所屬，故附列於此云。

translations.literal: Under Tang, the Academicians of the Hongwen and Jixian halls were separately subordinate to the Secretariat and Chancellery, while Hanlin Academicians alone belonged to no department; therefore they are appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Tang academicians of the Hongwen and Jixian halls fell under the Secretariat and Chancellery respectively, while Hanlin Academicians stood outside that structure—hence their treatment here.

sentences.zh: 三師三公太師、太傅、太保，各一人，是為三師；

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors and Three Dukes: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian, one each—these are the Three Preceptors;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors and Three Dukes. The Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Guardian, one each, constitute the Three Preceptors;

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒、司空，各一人，是為三公。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works, one each—these are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works, one each, constitute the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 皆正一品。

translations.literal: All were of the senior first rank.
translations.idiomatic: All held the senior first rank.

sentences.zh: 三師，天子所師法，無所總職，非其人則闕。

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors were those whom the Son of Heaven took as his models; they had no overarching duties, and if the man was not right the post was left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors were moral exemplars for the emperor, without administrative duties; the posts were left vacant when no suitable appointee existed.

sentences.zh: 三公，佐天子理陰陽、平邦國，無所不統。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes assisted the Son of Heaven in regulating yin and yang and settling the realm; nothing was outside their oversight.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes assisted the emperor in harmonizing cosmic order and governing the realm, with nominally universal oversight.

sentences.zh: 親王拜者不親事，祭祀闕則攝。

translations.literal: When a prince of the blood was appointed, he did not personally attend to affairs; if sacrifices were lacking he would act in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince of the blood received appointment, he did not handle routine affairs but might officiate at sacrifices when needed.

sentences.zh: 隋廢三師，貞觀十一年復置，與三公皆不設官屬。

translations.literal: Sui abolished the Three Preceptors; in the eleventh year of Zhenguan they were restored; neither they nor the Three Dukes had subordinate staff.
translations.idiomatic: Sui had abolished the Three Preceptors; they were restored in 637. Neither the Preceptors nor the Dukes had subordinate offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書省尚書令一人，正二品，掌典領百官。

translations.literal: Department of State Affairs: one Director, senior second rank, charged with overseeing the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs had one Director of senior second rank, charged with overseeing all officials.

sentences.zh: 其屬有六尚書：一曰吏部，二曰戶部，三曰禮部，四曰兵部，五曰刑部，六曰工部。

translations.literal: Its subordinates were six ministers: first Personnel, second Revenue, third Rites, fourth War, fifth Justice, and sixth Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under it were six ministries: Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Justice, and Works.

sentences.zh: 六尚書：兵部、吏部為前行，刑部、戶部為中行，工部、禮部為後行；

translations.literal: Among the six ministers, War and Personnel formed the leading row; Justice and Revenue the middle row; Works and Rites the rear row;
translations.idiomatic: Among the six ministries, War and Personnel formed the leading row, Justice and Revenue the middle row, and Works and Rites the rear row;

sentences.zh: 行總四司，以本行為頭司，餘為子司。

translations.literal: each row comprised four bureaus in all; the bureau of its own row was the head bureau, the rest subordinate bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: each row comprised four bureaus, with the ministry of that row as head bureau and the others as subordinate bureaus.

sentences.zh: 庶務皆會決焉。

translations.literal: All routine affairs were jointly decided there.
translations.idiomatic: All routine government business was decided there.

sentences.zh: 凡上之逮下，其制有六：一曰制，二曰敕，三曰冊，天子用之；

translations.literal: For communications from above reaching below, there were six forms: first proclamation, second edict, third investiture document—the Son of Heaven used these;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial communications downward took six forms: proclamation, edict, and investiture document, used by the emperor;

sentences.zh: 四曰令，皇太子用之；

translations.literal: fourth, order—the Heir Apparent used this;
translations.idiomatic: order, used by the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 五曰教，親王、公主用之；

translations.literal: fifth, instruction—princes of the blood and princesses used this;
translations.idiomatic: instruction, used by imperial princes and princesses;

sentences.zh: 六曰符，省下於州，州下於縣，縣下於鄉。

translations.literal: sixth, warrant—the department sent down to prefecture, prefecture to county, county to township.
translations.idiomatic: and warrant, issued from the department to prefecture, prefecture to county, and county to township.

sentences.zh: 下之達上，其制有六：一曰表，二曰狀，三曰牋，四曰啟，五曰辭，六曰牒。

translations.literal: For communications from below reaching above, there were six forms: first memorial, second report, third note, fourth communication, fifth petition, sixth dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Communications upward took six forms: memorial, report, note, communication, petition, and dispatch.

sentences.zh: 諸司相質，其制有三：一曰關，二曰刺，三曰移。

translations.literal: For mutual inquiry among offices, there were three forms: first pass, second query, third transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Inter-office communications took three forms: pass, query, and transfer.

sentences.zh: 凡授內外百司之事，皆印其發日為程，一曰受，二曰報。

translations.literal: For all matters assigned to the hundred offices within and without, the date of issue was stamped as the deadline: one day to receive, two days to report.
translations.idiomatic: All assignments to central and local offices were stamped with the issue date as deadline: one day to acknowledge receipt, two days to report back.

sentences.zh: 諸州計奏達京師，以事大小多少為之節。

translations.literal: Prefectural accounts and memorials reaching the capital were timed according to the size and quantity of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Deadlines for prefectural reports to the capital varied with the importance and volume of the matter.

sentences.zh: 凡符、移、關、牒，必遣於都省乃下。

translations.literal: All warrants, transfers, passes, and dispatches had to be sent through the central secretariat before being issued downward.
translations.idiomatic: Warrants, transfers, passes, and dispatches had to pass through the central secretariat before issuance.

sentences.zh: 天下大事不決者，皆上尚書省。

translations.literal: Great affairs of the realm that could not be decided were all referred up to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Major unresolved matters throughout the realm were referred to the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡制敕計奏之數、省符宣告之節，以歲終為斷。

translations.literal: The number of edicts and accounts and the deadlines for departmental warrants and proclamations were reckoned to the year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Tallies of edicts and memorials and deadlines for departmental communications were reckoned to the year's end.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改尚書省曰中臺，廢尚書令；

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, the Department of State Affairs was renamed Central Terrace and the Director abolished;
translations.idiomatic: In 662 the department was renamed Central Terrace and the post of Director abolished;

sentences.zh: 尚書曰太常伯，侍郎曰少常伯。

translations.literal: ministers were called Grand Constant Lords and vice ministers Lesser Constant Lords.
translations.idiomatic: ministers were titled Grand Constant Lord and vice ministers Lesser Constant Lord.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，改尚書省曰文昌臺，俄曰文昌都省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, the Department was renamed Wenchang Terrace, soon after Wenchang Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 it was renamed Wenchang Terrace, soon after Wenchang Directorate.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年曰都臺，長安三年曰中臺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong it was called Directorate Terrace; in the third year of Chang'an, Central Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In 685 it became Directorate Terrace; in 703, Central Terrace again.

sentences.zh: 左右僕射，各一人。

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Directors, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Vice Directors, one each.

sentences.zh: 從二品，掌統理六官，為令之貳，令闕則總省事，劾御史糾不當者。

translations.literal: Junior second rank; they governed and regulated the six ministries, served as deputies to the Director, and when the Director was vacant oversaw the department's affairs and impeached censors who prosecuted improperly.
translations.idiomatic: Junior second rank; they supervised the six ministries as the Director's deputies, managed the department when that post was vacant, and could impeach censors for improper prosecution.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改左右僕射曰左右匡政；

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, Left and Right Vice Directors were renamed Left and Right Rectifiers of Government;
translations.idiomatic: In 662 they were renamed Left and Right Rectifiers of Government;

sentences.zh: 光宅元年曰文昌左右相；

translations.literal: in the first year of Guangzhai, Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: in 684, Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors;

sentences.zh: 開元元年曰左、右丞相；

translations.literal: in the first year of Kaiyuan, Left and Right Chief Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: in 713, Left and Right Chief Ministers;

sentences.zh: 天寶元年復。

translations.literal: in the first year of Tianbao they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: in 742 the original titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 左丞一人，正四品上；

translations.literal: One Left Assistant Director, upper senior fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Left Assistant Director of upper senior fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 右丞一人，正四品下。

translations.literal: one Right Assistant Director, lower senior fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: one Right Assistant Director of lower senior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌辯六官之儀，糾正省內，劾御史舉不當者，吏部、戶部、禮部，左丞總焉；

translations.literal: They adjudicated the protocol of the six ministries, corrected matters within the department, and impeached censors who prosecuted improperly; Personnel, Revenue, and Rites were overseen by the Left Assistant Director;
translations.idiomatic: They regulated protocol among the six ministries, corrected internal irregularities, and could impeach censors for improper prosecution; the Left Assistant Director oversaw Personnel, Revenue, and Rites;

sentences.zh: 兵部、刑部、工部，右丞總焉。

translations.literal: War, Justice, and Works were overseen by the Right Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: the Right Assistant Director oversaw War, Justice, and Works.

sentences.zh: 郎中各一人，從五品上；

translations.literal: One director per side, junior fifth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: One director per side of junior fifth rank upper;

sentences.zh: 員外郎各一人，從六品上。

translations.literal: one vice director per side, junior sixth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: one vice director per side of junior sixth rank upper.

sentences.zh: 掌付諸司之務，舉稽違，署符目，知宿直，為丞之貳。

translations.literal: They assigned tasks to the various bureaus, reported delays and violations, signed warrant summaries, supervised night duty, and served as deputies to the assistant directors.
translations.idiomatic: They assigned work to the bureaus, reported delays and violations, signed warrant summaries, supervised night duty, and served as deputies to the assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 以都事受事發辰、察稽失、監印、給紙筆；

translations.literal: Chief clerks received documents and issued deadlines, inspected delays and errors, supervised seals, and supplied paper and brushes;
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks received documents and set deadlines, inspected delays and errors, supervised seals, and supplied stationery;

sentences.zh: 以主事、令史、書令史署覆文案，出符目；

translations.literal: section chiefs, clerks, and document clerks countersigned and reviewed documents and issued warrant summaries;
translations.idiomatic: section chiefs and clerks reviewed and countersigned documents and issued warrant summaries;

sentences.zh: 以亭長啟閉、傳禁約；

translations.literal: compound wardens opened and closed gates and transmitted prohibitions;
translations.idiomatic: compound wardens controlled access and transmitted security regulations;

sentences.zh: 以掌固守當倉庫及陳設。

translations.literal: storekeepers guarded warehouses and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: storekeepers guarded warehouses and ceremonial furnishings.

sentences.zh: 諸司皆如之。

translations.literal: All bureaus were likewise organized.
translations.idiomatic: All ministries followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 隋尚書省諸司郎及承務郎各一人，而廢左右司。

translations.literal: Under Sui the Department had one bureau director and one assistant director per bureau, and abolished the Left and Right Secretariat Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui each bureau had one director and one assistant director, and the Left and Right Secretariat Offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，改諸司郎為郎中，承務郎為員外郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, bureau directors were renamed directors and assistant directors renamed vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 bureau directors were renamed langzhong (directors) and assistant directors yuanwailang (vice directors).

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，復置左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Left and Right Secretariat Office directors were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 627 the Left and Right Secretariat Office directors were restored.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，改左右丞曰左右肅機，郎中曰左右承務，諸司郎中曰大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo, assistant directors were renamed Left and Right Rectifiers of Protocol, directors Left and Right Attendants, and bureau directors grandees.
translations.idiomatic: In 661 assistant directors became Left and Right Rectifiers of Protocol, directors Left and Right Attendants, and bureau directors grandees.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，復置員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, vice directors were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 689 the vice director posts were restored.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年省，明年復置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong they were abolished; the next year they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 705 they were abolished and restored the following year.

sentences.zh: 初有馹驛百人，掌乘傳送符，後廢。

translations.literal: At first there were one hundred relay couriers, charged with managing travel passes for relay transport; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Initially there were one hundred relay couriers who managed travel passes for the post-horse system; the office was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 都事各六人，從七品上；

translations.literal: Chief clerks, six each, junior seventh rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks, six per ministry, of junior seventh rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 主事各六人，從八品下。

translations.literal: section chiefs, six each, junior eighth rank lower.
translations.idiomatic: section chiefs, six per ministry, of junior eighth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 吏部考功、禮部主書皆如之。

translations.literal: The Examination Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel and the chief scribes of the Ministry of Rites were all likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Ministry's Bureau of Examination and the Rites Ministry's chief scribes followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 諸司主事，從九品上。

translations.literal: Bureau section chiefs, junior ninth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau section chiefs held junior ninth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 有令史各十八人，書令史各三十六人，亭長各六人，掌固各十四人。

translations.literal: There were clerks, eighteen each; document clerks, thirty-six each; compound wardens, six each; storekeepers, fourteen each.
translations.idiomatic: Each ministry had eighteen clerks, thirty-six document clerks, six compound wardens, and fourteen storekeepers.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel, one person, senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel had one minister of senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 侍郞二人，正四品上；

translations.literal: vice ministers, two persons, senior fourth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers of senior fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 郞中二人，正五品上；

translations.literal: directors, two persons, senior fifth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: two directors of senior fifth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 員外郞二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: vice directors, two persons, junior sixth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: two vice directors of junior sixth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 掌文選、勳封、考課之政。

translations.literal: They managed the affairs of civil selection, enfeoffment of merit, and performance evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw civil appointments, enfeoffments for merit, and official performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 以三銓之法官天下之材，以身、言、書、判，德行、才用、勞效較其優劣而定其留放，為之注擬。

translations.literal: By the law of the three selections they judged talent throughout the realm; by bodily presence, speech, calligraphy, and judgment, and by comparing moral conduct, talent and utility, and meritorious achievement, they weighed superiority and inferiority to decide retention or dismissal, and drafted nominations.
translations.idiomatic: Through the three-tier selection process they evaluated candidates empire-wide, testing presence, speech, calligraphy, and judgment and weighing character, competence, and service record to decide who would remain or be released, then drafted nominations accordingly.

sentences.zh: 五品以上，以名上而聽制授；

translations.literal: For fifth rank and above, names were submitted upward and appointments were made by imperial decree;
translations.idiomatic: For officials of fifth rank and above, nominations were sent to the throne and appointments were made by imperial decree;

sentences.zh: 六品以下，量資而任之。

translations.literal: for sixth rank and below, posts were assigned according to qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: for sixth rank and below, assignments were made according to qualifications.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰吏部，二曰司封，三曰司勳，四曰考功。

translations.literal: Its subordinates were four: first the Personnel Bureau, second the Bureau of Enfeoffments, third the Bureau of Merit, fourth the Bureau of Examination.
translations.idiomatic: It had four subordinate bureaus: Personnel, Enfeoffments, Merit, and Examination.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中，掌文官階品、朝集、祿賜，給其告身、假使，一人掌選補流外官。

translations.literal: Personnel Bureau director: charged with civil ranks and grades, court assemblies, salary and gifts, issuing commission certificates and leave permits; one person managed selection and appointment of officials outside the regular stream.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Bureau director managed civil ranks and grades, court assemblies, salaries and gifts, and the issuance of commission certificates and leave permits; one director also handled appointments for officials outside the regular stream.

sentences.zh: 員外郎二人。

translations.literal: Vice directors, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were two vice directors.

sentences.zh: 從六品上，一人判南曹。

translations.literal: Junior sixth rank upper; one person adjudicated the Southern Registry.
translations.idiomatic: Of junior sixth rank, upper grade; one supervised the Southern Registry.

sentences.zh: 皆為尚書、侍郎之貳。

translations.literal: All served as deputies to the minister and vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: All served as deputies to the minister and vice ministers.

sentences.zh: 凡文官九品，有正、有從，自正四品以下，有上、下，為三十等。

translations.literal: In all, civil officials had nine ranks, with regular and adjunct grades; from senior fourth rank downward there were upper and lower subdivisions, making thirty grades.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials were divided into nine ranks, each with regular and adjunct grades; from senior fourth rank down, upper and lower subdivisions yielded thirty grades in all.

sentences.zh: 凡文散階二十九：從一品曰開府儀同三司，正二品曰特進，從二品曰光祿大夫，正三品曰金紫光祿大夫，從三品曰銀青光祿大夫，正四品上曰正議大夫，正四品下曰通議大夫，從四品上曰太中大夫，從四品下曰中大夫，正五品上曰中散大夫，正五品下曰朝議大夫，從五品上曰朝請大夫，從五品下曰朝散大夫，正六品上曰朝議郎，正六品下曰承議郎，從六品上曰奉議郎，從六品下曰通直郎，正七品上曰朝請郎，正七品下曰宣德郎，從七品上曰朝散郎，從七品下曰宣義郎，正八品上曰給事郎，正八品下曰徵事郎，從八品上曰承奉郎，從八品下曰承務郎，正九品上曰儒林郎，正九品下曰登仕郎，從九品上曰文林郎，從九品下曰將仕郎。

translations.literal: In all there were twenty-nine honorary civil ranks: junior first rank was Kaifeng Yitong Sansi; senior second rank, Tejin; junior second rank, Guanglu Dafu; senior third rank, Jinzi Guanglu Dafu; junior third rank, Yinzi Qing Guanglu Dafu; senior fourth rank upper, Zhengyi Dafu; senior fourth rank lower, Tongyi Dafu; junior fourth rank upper, Taizhong Dafu; junior fourth rank lower, Zhong Dafu; senior fifth rank upper, Zhongsan Dafu; senior fifth rank lower, Chaoyi Dafu; junior fifth rank upper, Chaoqing Dafu; junior fifth rank lower, Chaosan Dafu; senior sixth rank upper, Chaoyilang; senior sixth rank lower, Chengyilang; junior sixth rank upper, Fengyilang; junior sixth rank lower, Tongzhilang; senior seventh rank upper, Chaoqinglang; senior seventh rank lower, Xuandelang; junior seventh rank upper, Chaosanlang; junior seventh rank lower, Xuanyilang; senior eighth rank upper, Jishilang; senior eighth rank lower, Zhengshilang; junior eighth rank upper, Chengfenglang; junior eighth rank lower, Chengwulang; senior ninth rank upper, Rulinlang; senior ninth rank lower, Dengshilang; junior ninth rank upper, Wenlinlang; junior ninth rank lower, Jiangshilang.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-nine honorary civil ranks, from Junior First Rank, Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Equal Privilege to the Three Dukes, down through Special Advancement, Grand Masters for Splendid and Glorious Happiness with golden or silver seals, the various Grand Masters and Gentlemen of court counsel and discussion, to Junior Ninth Rank, Gentleman Awaiting Office.

sentences.zh: 自四品，皆番上於吏部；

translations.literal: From fourth rank downward, all reported in rotation at the Ministry of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: From fourth rank down, all officials reported for rotating duty at the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 不上者，歲輸資錢，三品以上六百，六品以下一千，水、旱、蟲、霜減半資。

translations.literal: those who did not report paid annual capital-residence fees: six hundred for third rank and above, one thousand for sixth rank and below; flood, drought, pest, and frost disasters halved the fee.
translations.idiomatic: those who did not report paid an annual capital-residence fee—six hundred cash for third rank and above, one thousand for sixth rank and below—with the fee halved in years of flood, drought, pestilence, or frost.

sentences.zh: 有文藝樂京上者，每州七人；

translations.literal: Those with literary talent who preferred residence in the capital, seven per prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Officials with literary talent who preferred to remain in the capital were limited to seven per prefecture;

sentences.zh: 六十不樂簡選者，罷輸。

translations.literal: at age sixty, those unwilling to undergo selection examination were exempted from paying fees.
translations.idiomatic: at sixty, those who no longer wished to undergo selection were exempt from the fee.

sentences.zh: 勳官亦如之。

translations.literal: Merit-title holders were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same rules applied to holders of merit titles.

sentences.zh: 以征鎮功得護軍以上者，納資減三之一。

translations.literal: Those who through frontier campaign merit received Defender of the State or above had their fees reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Those who earned Defender of the State or higher through frontier service paid one-third less.

sentences.zh: 凡流外九品，取其書、計、時務，其校試、銓注，與流內略同，謂之小選。

translations.literal: In all, outside the regular stream there were nine ranks; writing, accounting, and current affairs were tested; verification examinations and selection nominations were broadly the same as within the regular stream—this was called the minor selection.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the regular stream there were nine ranks, with candidates tested in writing, accounting, and practical affairs; verification and nomination followed much the same procedure as the regular stream and was called the minor selection.

sentences.zh: 吏部主事四人，司封主事二人，司勳主事四人，考功主事三人。

translations.literal: Personnel Bureau section chiefs four, Enfeoffments Bureau section chiefs two, Merit Bureau section chiefs four, Examination Bureau section chiefs three.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Bureau had four section chiefs, Enfeoffments two, Merit four, and Examination three.

sentences.zh: 武德五年改選部曰吏部，七年省侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude the Selection Department was renamed Ministry of Personnel; in the seventh year the vice minister post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 622 the Selection Department was renamed the Ministry of Personnel; in 624 the vice minister post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年復置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in 628.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年改吏部曰司列，主爵曰司封，考功曰司績。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo the Ministry of Personnel was renamed Directorate of Arrangement, Bureau of Nobility renamed Bureau of Enfeoffments, and Bureau of Examination renamed Bureau of Merit Records.
translations.idiomatic: In 661 the ministry became the Directorate of Arrangement, the Bureau of Nobility became the Bureau of Enfeoffments, and the Bureau of Examination became the Bureau of Merit Records.

sentences.zh: 武后光宅元年改吏部曰天官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu the Ministry of Personnel was renamed Heavenly Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 Empress Wu renamed the ministry the Heavenly Office.

sentences.zh: 垂拱元年改主爵曰司封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuigong the Bureau of Nobility was renamed Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: In 685 the Bureau of Nobility was renamed the Bureau of Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載改吏部曰文部，至德二載復舊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao the Ministry of Personnel was renamed Literary Department; in the second year of Zhide the former name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 it was renamed the Literary Department; in 757 the original name was restored.

sentences.zh: 有吏部令史三十人，書令史六十人；

translations.literal: There were thirty Ministry of Personnel clerks and sixty document clerks;
translations.idiomatic: The ministry had thirty clerks and sixty document clerks;

sentences.zh: 制書令史十四人；

translations.literal: fourteen edict clerks;
translations.idiomatic: fourteen edict clerks;

sentences.zh: 甲庫令史十三人，亭長八人，掌固十二人；

translations.literal: thirteen registry-A clerks, eight compound wardens, twelve storekeepers;
translations.idiomatic: thirteen registry clerks for the A archive, eight compound wardens, and twelve storekeepers;

sentences.zh: 司封令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Enfeoffments Bureau clerks four, document clerks nine, storekeepers four;
translations.idiomatic: the Enfeoffments Bureau had four clerks, nine document clerks, and four storekeepers;

sentences.zh: 司勳令史三十三人，書令史六十七人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Merit Bureau clerks thirty-three, document clerks sixty-seven, storekeepers four;
translations.idiomatic: the Merit Bureau had thirty-three clerks, sixty-seven document clerks, and four storekeepers;

sentences.zh: 考功令史十五人，書令史三十人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Examination Bureau clerks fifteen, document clerks thirty, storekeepers four.
translations.idiomatic: the Examination Bureau had fifteen clerks, thirty document clerks, and four storekeepers.

sentences.zh: 司封郎中一人，從五品上；

translations.literal: Enfeoffments Bureau director, one person, junior fifth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: The Enfeoffments Bureau had one director of junior fifth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人，從六品上；

translations.literal: vice director, one person, junior sixth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: one vice director of junior sixth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 諸郎中、員外郎品皆如之。

translations.literal: directors and vice directors of all bureaus had ranks likewise.
translations.idiomatic: directors and vice directors of the other bureaus held the same ranks.

sentences.zh: 掌封命、朝會、賜予之級。

translations.literal: They managed enfeoffment patents, court assemblies, and grades of bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: They managed patents of enfeoffment, court assemblies, and the grades of imperial grants.

sentences.zh: 凡爵九等：一曰王，食邑萬戶，正一品；

translations.literal: In all there were nine ranks of nobility: first, prince, fief of ten thousand households, senior first rank;
translations.idiomatic: Nobility comprised nine ranks: first, Prince, with a fief of ten thousand households, senior first rank;

sentences.zh: 二曰嗣王、郡王，食邑五千戶，從一品；

translations.literal: second, succession prince and commandery prince, fief of five thousand households, junior first rank;
translations.idiomatic: second, Succession Prince and Commandery Prince, five thousand households, junior first rank;

sentences.zh: 三曰國公，食邑三千戶，從一品；

translations.literal: third, state duke, fief of three thousand households, junior first rank;
translations.idiomatic: third, State Duke, three thousand households, junior first rank;

sentences.zh: 四曰開國郡公，食邑二千戶，正二品；

translations.literal: fourth, founding commandery duke, fief of two thousand households, senior second rank;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, Founding Commandery Duke, two thousand households, senior second rank;

sentences.zh: 五曰開國縣公，食邑千五百戶，從二品；

translations.literal: fifth, founding county duke, fief of one thousand five hundred households, junior second rank;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, Founding County Duke, one thousand five hundred households, junior second rank;

sentences.zh: 六曰開國縣侯，食邑千戶，從三品；

translations.literal: sixth, founding county marquis, fief of one thousand households, junior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, Founding County Marquis, one thousand households, junior third rank;

sentences.zh: 七曰開國縣伯，食邑七百戶，正四品上；

translations.literal: seventh, founding county earl, fief of seven hundred households, senior fourth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, Founding County Earl, seven hundred households, senior fourth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 八曰開國縣子，食邑五百戶，正五品上；

translations.literal: eighth, founding county viscount, fief of five hundred households, senior fifth rank upper;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, Founding County Viscount, five hundred households, senior fifth rank, upper grade;

sentences.zh: 九曰開國縣男，食邑三百戶，從五品上。

translations.literal: ninth, founding county baron, fief of three hundred households, junior fifth rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: ninth, Founding County Baron, three hundred households, junior fifth rank, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 皇兄弟、皇子，皆封國為親王；

translations.literal: Imperial brothers and sons of the emperor were all enfeoffed with a state as princes of the blood;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's brothers and sons were all enfeoffed with a state and titled Princes of the Blood;

sentences.zh: 皇太子子，為郡王；

translations.literal: sons of the crown prince were made commandery princes;
translations.idiomatic: sons of the crown prince were made commandery princes;

sentences.zh: 親王之子，承嫡者為嗣王，諸子為郡公，以恩進者封郡王；

translations.literal: sons of princes of the blood: the heir by primogeniture became succession prince, other sons became commandery dukes, and those promoted by grace were enfeoffed as commandery princes;
translations.idiomatic: among a prince's sons, the legitimate heir became Succession Prince, other sons became commandery dukes, and those promoted by special grace were enfeoffed as commandery princes;

sentences.zh: 襲郡王、嗣王者，封國公。

translations.literal: those inheriting commandery princes or succession princes were enfeoffed as state dukes.
translations.idiomatic: those who inherited commandery princely or succession princely titles were enfeoffed as state dukes.

sentences.zh: 皇姑為大長公主，正一品；

translations.literal: The emperor's paternal aunts were titled grand long princesses, senior first rank;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's paternal aunts were titled Grand Long Princesses, senior first rank;

sentences.zh: 姊妹為長公主，女為公主，皆視一品；

translations.literal: sisters were long princesses, daughters were princesses—all treated as first rank;
translations.idiomatic: sisters were Long Princesses and daughters were Princesses—all accorded first rank;

sentences.zh: 皇太子女為郡主，從一品；

translations.literal: daughters of the crown prince were commandery princesses, junior first rank;
translations.idiomatic: daughters of the crown prince were Commandery Princesses, junior first rank;

sentences.zh: 親王女為縣主，從二品。

translations.literal: daughters of princes of the blood were county princesses, junior second rank.
translations.idiomatic: daughters of princes of the blood were County Princesses, junior second rank.

sentences.zh: 凡王、公十五以上，預朝集，宗親女婦、諸王長女月二參。

translations.literal: In all, princes and dukes aged fifteen and above attended court assemblies; female imperial relatives and eldest daughters of princes attended court twice monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes aged fifteen and above attended court assemblies; female imperial relatives and each prince's eldest daughter attended court twice a month.

sentences.zh: 內命婦，一品母為正四品郡君，二品母為從四品郡君，三品、四品母為正五品縣君。

translations.literal: For inner titled ladies: a first-rank official's mother was a commandery lady of senior fourth rank, a second-rank official's mother a commandery lady of junior fourth rank, and a third- or fourth-rank official's mother a county lady of senior fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Among inner titled ladies, the mother of a first-rank official was a Commandery Lady of senior fourth rank, of a second-rank official a Commandery Lady of junior fourth rank, and of a third- or fourth-rank official a County Lady of senior fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡諸王、公主、外戚之家，卜、祝、占、相不入門。

translations.literal: In all, at the households of princes, princesses, and imperial affines, diviners, prayer masters, augurs, and physiognomists were forbidden entry.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners, prayer masters, augurs, and physiognomers were forbidden to enter the households of princes, princesses, and imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 王妃、公主、郡縣主嫠居有子者，不再嫁。

translations.literal: Widowed princess consorts, princesses, and commandery or county princesses who had sons were not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed princess consorts, princesses, and commandery or county princesses who had sons were forbidden to remarry.

sentences.zh: 凡外命婦有六：王、嗣王、郡王之母、妻為妃，文武官一品、國公之母、妻為國夫人，三品以上母、妻為郡夫人，四品母、妻為郡君，五品母、妻為縣君，勳官四品有封者母、妻為鄉君。

translations.literal: In all there were six categories of outer titled ladies: mothers and wives of princes, succession princes, and commandery princes were consorts; mothers and wives of civil and military officials of first rank and state dukes were state ladies; mothers and wives of third rank and above were commandery madams; mothers and wives of fourth rank were commandery ladies; mothers and wives of fifth rank were county ladies; mothers and wives of merit-title holders of fourth rank with enfeoffment were township ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Outer titled ladies fell into six categories: mothers and wives of princes, succession princes, and commandery princes were Consorts; mothers and wives of first-rank civil and military officials and state dukes were State Ladies; those of third rank and above were Commandery Madams; those of fourth rank were Commandery Ladies; those of fifth rank were County Ladies; and mothers and wives of enfeoffed fourth-rank merit-title holders were Township Ladies.

sentences.zh: 凡外命婦朝參，視夫、子之品。

translations.literal: In all, outer titled ladies attending court were treated according to the rank of their husbands or sons.
translations.idiomatic: Outer titled ladies attended court according to the rank of their husband or son.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃三品以上母、妻授封以制。

translations.literal: For foreign tributary officials of third rank and above, enfeoffment of mothers and wives followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For foreign tributary officials of third rank and above, titles for mothers and wives were granted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 流外技術官，不封母、妻。

translations.literal: Technical officials outside the regular stream did not enfeoff mothers or wives.
translations.idiomatic: Technical officials outside the regular stream could not obtain titles for their mothers or wives.

sentences.zh: 親王，孺人二人，視正五品，媵十人，視從六品；

translations.literal: Princes of the blood: two ladies, treated as senior fifth rank; ten secondary consorts, treated as junior sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the Blood had two Ladies, accorded senior fifth rank, and ten secondary consorts, accorded junior sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 二品，媵八人，視正七品；

translations.literal: second rank, eight secondary consorts, treated as senior seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: second-rank officials had eight secondary consorts, accorded senior seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 國公及三品，媵六人，視從七品；

translations.literal: state dukes and third rank, six secondary consorts, treated as junior seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: state dukes and third-rank officials had six secondary consorts, accorded junior seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 四品，媵四人，視正八品；

translations.literal: fourth rank, four secondary consorts, treated as senior eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: fourth-rank officials had four secondary consorts, accorded senior eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 五品，媵三人，視從八品。

translations.literal: fifth rank, three secondary consorts, treated as junior eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: fifth-rank officials had three secondary consorts, accorded junior eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡置媵，上其數，補以告身。

translations.literal: In all, when appointing secondary consorts, their number was reported upward and they were supplied with commission certificates.
translations.idiomatic: When appointing secondary consorts, the number was reported to the authorities and commission certificates were issued.

sentences.zh: 散官三品以上，皆置媵。

translations.literal: Honorary officials of third rank and above all had secondary consorts appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Honorary officials of third rank and above were all entitled to secondary consorts.

sentences.zh: 凡封戶，三丁以上為率，歲租三之一入于朝庭。

translations.literal: In all, for fief households, households with three adult males or more served as the standard unit; one-third of the annual land tax entered the court.
translations.idiomatic: Fief income was calculated in household units of three adult males or more; one-third of each household's annual land tax went to the court.

sentences.zh: 食實封者，得真戶，分食諸州。

translations.literal: Those receiving actual fief income obtained real households and shared sustenance among the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Recipients of actual fief income received real households, with income distributed across the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 皇后、諸王、公主食邑，皆有課戶。

translations.literal: The empress, princes, and princesses all had assessed households for their fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, princes, and princesses all drew fief income from assessed households.

sentences.zh: 名山、大川、畿內之地，皆不以封。

translations.literal: Famous mountains, great rivers, and lands within the capital circuit were never granted as fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Famous mountains, great rivers, and lands within the capital region were never granted as fiefs.

sentences.zh: 司勳郎中一人，員外郎二人，掌官吏勳級。

translations.literal: Merit Bureau director one person, vice directors two persons, managing officials' merit grades.
translations.idiomatic: The Merit Bureau had one director and two vice directors, who managed officials' merit grades.

sentences.zh: 凡十有二轉為上柱國，視正二品；

translations.literal: In all, twelve rotations made Upper Pillar of State, treated as senior second rank;
translations.idiomatic: Twelve rotations conferred Upper Pillar of State, accorded senior second rank;

sentences.zh: 十有一轉為柱國，視從二品；

translations.literal: eleven rotations made Pillar of State, treated as junior second rank;
translations.idiomatic: eleven rotations conferred Pillar of State, accorded junior second rank;

sentences.zh: 十轉為上護軍，視正三品；

translations.literal: ten rotations made Upper Defender of the State, treated as senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: ten rotations conferred Upper Defender of the State, accorded senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 九轉為護軍，視從三品；

translations.literal: nine rotations made Defender of the State, treated as junior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: nine rotations conferred Defender of the State, accorded junior third rank;

sentences.zh: 八轉為上輕車都尉，視正四品；

translations.literal: eight rotations made Upper Chief Commandant of Light Chariots, treated as senior fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: eight rotations conferred Upper Chief Commandant of Light Chariots, accorded senior fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 七轉為輕車都尉，視從四品；

translations.literal: seven rotations made Chief Commandant of Light Chariots, treated as junior fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: seven rotations conferred Chief Commandant of Light Chariots, accorded junior fourth rank;

sentences.zh: 六轉為上騎都尉，視正五品；

translations.literal: six rotations made Upper Commandant of Cavalry, treated as senior fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: six rotations conferred Upper Commandant of Cavalry, accorded senior fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 五轉為騎都尉，視從五品；

translations.literal: five rotations made Commandant of Cavalry, treated as junior fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: five rotations conferred Commandant of Cavalry, accorded junior fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 四轉為驍騎尉，視正六品；

translations.literal: four rotations made Commandant of Valiant Cavalry, treated as senior sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: four rotations conferred Commandant of Valiant Cavalry, accorded senior sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 三轉為飛騎尉，視從六品；

translations.literal: three rotations made Commandant of Flying Cavalry, treated as junior sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: three rotations conferred Commandant of Flying Cavalry, accorded junior sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 二轉為雲騎尉，視正七品；

translations.literal: two rotations made Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, treated as senior seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: two rotations conferred Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, accorded senior seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 一轉為武騎尉，視從七品。

translations.literal: one rotation made Commandant of Martial Cavalry, treated as junior seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: one rotation conferred Commandant of Martial Cavalry, accorded junior seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 凡以功授者，覆實然後奏擬，戰功則計殺獲之數。

translations.literal: In all, for conferral by merit, verification was completed before memorializing nomination; for battlefield merit the number of kills and captures was reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Merit conferrals required verification before nomination was submitted; battlefield merit was calculated by the number of enemies killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 堅城苦戰，功第一者，三轉。

translations.literal: For holding a city through bitter fighting, the one ranked first in merit received three rotations.
translations.idiomatic: For holding a city through bitter fighting, the highest merit rating earned three rotations.

sentences.zh: 出少擊多，曰上陣；

translations.literal: Going out with fewer to strike more was called a superior engagement;
translations.idiomatic: Engaging with fewer troops against more was termed a superior engagement;

sentences.zh: 兵數相當，曰中陣；

translations.literal: when troop numbers were equal, it was called a medium engagement;
translations.idiomatic: when forces were equal, a medium engagement;

sentences.zh: 出多擊少，曰下陣；

translations.literal: going out with more to strike fewer was called an inferior engagement;
translations.idiomatic: engaging with more troops against fewer, an inferior engagement;

sentences.zh: 矢石未交，陷堅突眾，敵因而敗者，曰跳盪。

translations.literal: before arrows and stones had been exchanged, breaking through strong positions and charging the mass of the enemy so that the foe was thereby defeated was called a sally.
translations.idiomatic: A charge through strong positions against the enemy mass before missiles were exchanged, causing the enemy to break, was called a sally.

sentences.zh: 殺獲十之四，曰上獲；

translations.literal: Killing and capturing four-tenths, is called superior capture;
translations.idiomatic: A kill-and-capture ratio of four-tenths was rated superior capture;

sentences.zh: 十之二，曰中獲；

translations.literal: two-tenths, is called medium capture;
translations.idiomatic: two-tenths, medium capture;

sentences.zh: 十之一，曰下獲。

translations.literal: one-tenth, is called inferior capture.
translations.idiomatic: one-tenth, inferior capture.

sentences.zh: 凡酬功之等：見任、前資、常選，曰上資；

translations.literal: In all, the grades for rewarding merit: incumbents, those with prior qualifications, and regular selection candidates were called upper qualification;
translations.idiomatic: Merit rewards were graded by recipient status: incumbents, holders of prior qualifications, and regular selection candidates counted as upper qualification;

sentences.zh: 文武散官、衞官、勳官五品以上，曰次資；

translations.literal: civil and military prestige-rank holders, guard officials, and merit-title holders of fifth rank and above were called second qualification;
translations.idiomatic: civil and military prestige-rank holders, guard officials, and merit-title holders of fifth rank and above as second qualification;

sentences.zh: 五品以上子孫，上柱國、柱國子，勳官六品以下，曰下資；

translations.literal: descendants of fifth rank and above, sons of Upper Pillar of State and Pillar of State, and merit-title holders of sixth rank and below were called lower qualification;
translations.idiomatic: descendants of fifth-rank officials and above, sons of Upper Pillar of State and Pillar of State holders, and merit-title holders of sixth rank and below as lower qualification;

sentences.zh: 白丁、衞士，曰無資。

translations.literal: commoners and guardsmen were called no qualification.
translations.idiomatic: commoners and guardsmen as no qualification.

sentences.zh: 跳盪人，上資加二階，次資、下資、無資以次降。

translations.literal: For sally fighters, upper qualification added two grades; second, lower, and no qualification were reduced in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: Sally fighters earned two extra grade steps at upper qualification; rewards for second, lower, and no qualification diminished in turn.

sentences.zh: 凡上陣：上獲五轉，中獲四轉，下獲三轉，第二、第三等遞降焉。

translations.literal: In all, for superior engagements: superior capture received five rotations, medium capture four rotations, inferior capture three rotations; second and third grades were progressively reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In superior engagements, superior capture earned five rotations, medium capture four, and inferior capture three; second- and third-tier recipients were reduced step by step.

sentences.zh: 中陣之上獲視上陣之中獲，中獲視上陣之下獲，下獲兩轉。

translations.literal: In medium engagements, superior capture was treated as medium capture in a superior engagement; medium capture as inferior capture in a superior engagement; inferior capture received two rotations.
translations.idiomatic: In medium engagements, superior capture counted as medium capture in a superior engagement, medium capture as inferior capture in a superior engagement, and inferior capture two rotations.

sentences.zh: 下陣之上獲視中陣之中獲，中獲視中陣之下獲，下獲一轉。

translations.literal: In inferior engagements, superior capture was treated as medium capture in a medium engagement; medium capture as inferior capture in a medium engagement; inferior capture received one rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In inferior engagements, superior capture counted as medium capture in a medium engagement, medium capture as inferior capture in a medium engagement, and inferior capture one rotation.

sentences.zh: 破蠻、獠，上陣上獲，比兩番降二轉。

translations.literal: In defeating Man and Liao tribes, for superior engagement with superior capture, compared with the standard, two rotations were deducted.
translations.idiomatic: Victories over Man and Liao peoples, even at superior engagement with superior capture, were reduced by two rotations from the standard award.

sentences.zh: 凡勳官九百人，無職任者，番上於兵部，視遠近為十二番，以彊幹者為番頭，留宿衞者為番，月上。

translations.literal: In all, nine hundred merit-title holders without office assignments reported in rotation at the Ministry of War; according to distance they were divided into twelve rotations; the ablest served as rotation heads; those remaining for palace guard duty formed the rotation and reported upward monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Nine hundred merit-title holders without active posts rotated through the Ministry of War, apportioned into twelve shifts by distance; the strongest led each shift, palace-guard detachments formed the monthly rotation, and returns were filed each month.

sentences.zh: 外州分五番，主城門、倉庫，執刀。

translations.literal: Outer prefectures were divided into five rotations, chiefly guarding city gates and storehouses and bearing swords.
translations.idiomatic: Outer prefectures were split into five rotations, mainly guarding gates and granaries with drawn blades.

sentences.zh: 上柱國以下番上四年，驍騎尉以下番上五年，簡於兵部，授散官；

translations.literal: From Upper Pillar of State downward, rotation duty lasted four years; from Commandant of Valiant Cavalry downward, five years; selection was made at the Ministry of War and prestige rank was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: From Upper Pillar of State down, four years of rotation duty; from Commandant of Valiant Cavalry down, five; candidates were screened at the Ministry of War and given prestige rank.

sentences.zh: 不第者，五品以上復番上四年，六品以下五年，簡如初；

translations.literal: Those who did not pass selection: fifth rank and above again performed rotation duty for four years, sixth rank and below for five years, with selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed selection served another rotation—four years for fifth rank and above, five for sixth and below—then faced the same screening again.

sentences.zh: 再不中者，十二年則番上六年，八年則番上四年。

translations.literal: Those who failed twice: after twelve years, rotation duty was six years; after eight years, rotation duty was four years.
translations.idiomatic: After two failures, rotation terms were shortened: twelve years' service meant six years on rotation; eight years meant four.

sentences.zh: 勳至上柱國有餘，則授周以上親，無者賜物。

translations.literal: When merit reached Upper Pillar of State with surplus, it was conferred on relatives within the five degrees of kinship; if there were none, goods were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Merit accumulated beyond Upper Pillar of State could pass to relatives within the five degrees of mourning; where no kin qualified, the surplus was paid out in goods.

sentences.zh: 太常音聲人，得五品以上勳，非征討功不除簿。

translations.literal: Musicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices who received merit of fifth rank and above were not removed from the register unless the merit came from campaign service.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians granted fifth-rank merit or above kept their registry entries—and thus their exemptions—only when the merit arose from active campaigning.

sentences.zh: 諸州授勳人，歲第勳之高下，三月一報戶部，有蠲免必驗。

translations.literal: In all prefectures conferring merit, the high and low of merit conferred each year was reported to the Ministry of Revenue once every three months; any tax exemptions had to be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures granting merit titles ranked recipients annually and reported to the Ministry of Revenue quarterly; every claimed exemption required verification.

sentences.zh: 考功郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌文武百官功過、善惡之考法及其行狀。

translations.literal: Director and vice director of the Bureau of Examination, one each, managed the examination methods for the merits and faults, good and ill, of civil and military officials of all ranks, and their conduct records.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Examination had one director and one vice director, charged with the rules for evaluating officials' merits and faults and with compiling their conduct records.

sentences.zh: 若死而傳於史官、謚于太常，則以其行狀質其當不；

translations.literal: If after death one was recorded by the historiographers or given a posthumous title by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then by the conduct record one verified whether it was fitting or not;
translations.idiomatic: When the historiographers took up a man's record or the Court of Imperial Sacrifices weighed a posthumous name, his conduct record was the standard of proof;

sentences.zh: 其欲銘于碑者，則會百官議其宜述者以聞，報其家。

translations.literal: for those wishing an inscription on a stele, officials were assembled to discuss what should be narrated and report upward, and the family was notified.
translations.idiomatic: those seeking a stele inscription had their case debated in assembly, the recommended text reported upward, and the family informed.

sentences.zh: 其考法，凡百司之長，歲較其屬功過，差以九等，大合眾而讀之。

translations.literal: As for the examination method: in all, the heads of offices each year compared the merits and faults of their subordinates, differentiated them into nine grades, and read them aloud before the assembled multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Each year department heads rated subordinates' merits and faults, sorted them into nine grades, and read the results aloud in full assembly.

sentences.zh: 流內之官，敍以四善：一曰德義有聞，二曰清慎明著，三曰公平可稱，四曰恪勤匪懈。

translations.literal: For flow-within officials, account was taken of four virtues: first, virtue and righteousness widely known; second, purity and caution clearly manifest; third, fairness worthy of praise; fourth, dutiful diligence without slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Flow-within officials were judged on four virtues: repute for integrity, conspicuous probity, acknowledged fairness, and tireless diligence.

sentences.zh: 善狀之外有二十七最：一曰獻可替否，拾遺補闕，為近侍之最；

translations.literal: Beyond records of virtue there were twenty-seven supreme merits: first, offering approval and replacing disapproval, gathering omissions and filling gaps, was the supreme merit for close attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Alongside virtue ratings stood twenty-seven supreme merits: first, approving what was sound, rejecting what was not, and mending every gap— the supreme merit for close attendants;

sentences.zh: 二曰銓衡人物，擢盡才良，為選司之最；

translations.literal: second, weighing persons and promoting all worthy talent, was the supreme merit for the Selection Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: second, weighing candidates and elevating every able man— the supreme merit for the Selection Bureau;

sentences.zh: 三曰揚清激濁，褒貶必當，為考校之最；

translations.literal: third, raising the pure and stirring the turbid, with praise and blame always apt, was the supreme merit for examiners;
translations.idiomatic: third, elevating the upright and exposing the corrupt, with praise and censure always apt— the supreme merit for examining officers;

sentences.zh: 四曰禮制儀式，動合經典，為禮官之最；

translations.literal: fourth, rites and ceremonial forms in motion conforming to the classics, was the supreme merit for rites officials;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, rites and ceremony performed in faithful accord with the classics— the supreme merit for rites officials;

sentences.zh: 五曰音律克諧，不失節奏，為樂官之最；

translations.literal: fifth, tones and pitch harmonizing, rhythm never lost, was the supreme merit for music officials;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, pitch and measure kept in harmony, rhythm never lost— the supreme merit for music officials;

sentences.zh: 六曰決斷不滯，與奪合理，為判事之最；

translations.literal: sixth, decisions not delayed, grants and denials reasonable, was the supreme merit for adjudicators;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, judgments rendered without delay, awards and refusals always reasonable— the supreme merit for adjudicators;

sentences.zh: 七曰部統有方，警守無失，為宿衞之最；

translations.literal: seventh, command with method, guard and watch without lapse, was the supreme merit for palace guards;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, command exercised with order, watches kept without breach— the supreme merit for palace guards;

sentences.zh: 八曰兵士調習，戎裝充備，為督領之最；

translations.literal: eighth, soldiers drilled and exercised, military gear fully supplied, was the supreme merit for supervisors;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, troops drilled and equipped, armor and arms fully at hand— the supreme merit for military supervisors;

sentences.zh: 九曰推鞫得情，處斷平允，為法官之最；

translations.literal: ninth, interrogation reaching the truth of the case, judgment and sentence fair and even, was the supreme merit for judges;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, interrogation that reached the truth, sentencing fair and even— the supreme merit for judges;

sentences.zh: 十曰讎校精審，明於刊定，為校正之最；

translations.literal: tenth, collation precise and thorough, clear in editing and fixing texts, was the supreme merit for proofreaders;
translations.idiomatic: tenth, collation exact and thorough, emendation lucid and sure— the supreme merit for textual proofreaders;

sentences.zh: 十一曰承旨敷奏，吐納明敏，為宣納之最；

translations.literal: eleventh, receiving the imperial will and presenting memorials, speech clear and nimble, was the supreme merit for memorial presenters;
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, receiving the throne's intent and presenting memorials with clarity and dispatch— the supreme merit for memorial presenters;

sentences.zh: 十二曰訓導有方，生徒充業，為學官之最；

translations.literal: twelfth, instruction with method, students completing their studies, was the supreme merit for academic officials;
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, instruction well ordered, students completing their course— the supreme merit for academy officers;

sentences.zh: 十三曰賞罰嚴明，攻戰必勝，為軍將之最；

translations.literal: thirteenth, rewards and punishments strict and clear, attacks and battles always victorious, was the supreme merit for military generals;
translations.idiomatic: thirteenth, rewards and punishments stern and lucid, every attack crowned with victory— the supreme merit for field commanders;

sentences.zh: 十四曰禮義興行，肅清所部，為政教之最；
