translations.literal: fourteenth, rites and righteousness flourishing in practice, the department governed in austere order, was the supreme merit for civil administrators;
translations.idiomatic: fourteenth, rites and righteousness actively upheld, the jurisdiction kept in sober order— the supreme merit for civil administrators;

sentences.zh: 十五曰詳錄典正，詞理兼舉，為文史之最；

translations.literal: fifteenth, records detailed and correct, language and reasoning both upheld, was the supreme merit for literary and historical officials;
translations.idiomatic: fifteenth, records exact and authoritative, diction and argument equally strong— the supreme merit for literary and historical officers;

sentences.zh: 十六曰訪察精審，彈舉必當，為糾正之最；

translations.literal: sixteenth, investigation precise and thorough, impeachments always apt, was the supreme merit for censors;
translations.idiomatic: sixteenth, inquiry precise and penetrating, impeachments always well aimed— the supreme merit for censors;

sentences.zh: 十七曰明於勘覆，稽失無隱，為句檢之最；

translations.literal: seventeenth, clear in audit and review, errors examined without concealment, was the supreme merit for auditors;
translations.idiomatic: seventeenth, audits conducted with clarity, every lapse traced and exposed— the supreme merit for auditors;

sentences.zh: 十八曰職事脩理，供承彊濟，為監掌之最；

translations.literal: eighteenth, official duties well ordered, supplies furnished strong and timely, was the supreme merit for superintendents;
translations.idiomatic: eighteenth, duties kept in good repair, provisions supplied abundantly and on time— the supreme merit for superintendents;

sentences.zh: 十九曰功課皆充，丁匠無怨，為役使之最；

translations.literal: nineteenth, labor quotas all fulfilled, corvée workers without complaint, was the supreme merit for labor supervisors;
translations.idiomatic: nineteenth, every labor quota met, corvée workers left without grievance— the supreme merit for labor overseers;

sentences.zh: 二十曰耕耨以時，收穫成課，為屯官之最；

translations.literal: twentieth, plowing and weeding at the proper season, harvest meeting quota, was the supreme merit for garrison agricultural officials;
translations.idiomatic: twentieth, fields tilled and tended in season, harvests meeting their quotas— the supreme merit for garrison agricultural officers;

sentences.zh: 二十一曰謹於蓋藏，明於出納，為倉庫之最；

translations.literal: twenty-first, careful in storage and covering, clear in disbursement and receipt, was the supreme merit for granary officials;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-first, stores kept with care, receipts and issues handled with precision— the supreme merit for granary officers;

sentences.zh: 二十二曰推步盈虛，究理精密，為曆官之最；

translations.literal: twenty-second, calculating celestial cycles of waxing and waning, reasoning pursued to precision, was the supreme merit for calendar officials;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-second, celestial cycles calculated with exactitude, theory pursued to the finest point— the supreme merit for calendar officers;

sentences.zh: 二十三曰占候醫卜，效驗多者，為方術之最；

translations.literal: twenty-third, divination, medicine, and augury with many verified results, was the supreme merit for technical specialists;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-third, divination, medicine, and augury with abundant verified results— the supreme merit for technical specialists;

sentences.zh: 二十四曰檢察有方，行旅無壅，為關津之最；

translations.literal: twenty-fourth, inspection conducted with method, travelers not obstructed, was the supreme merit for pass officials;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-fourth, inspection orderly and effective, travelers never impeded— the supreme merit for pass and ferry officers;

sentences.zh: 二十五曰市廛弗擾，姦濫不行，為市司之最；

translations.literal: twenty-fifth, market stalls not disturbed, fraud and abuse not practiced, was the supreme merit for market officials;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-fifth, markets left untroubled, fraud and abuse kept out— the supreme merit for market superintendents;

sentences.zh: 二十六曰牧養肥碩，蕃息孳多，為牧官之最；

translations.literal: twenty-sixth, herds fat and thriving, breeding prolific, was the supreme merit for pastoral officials;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-sixth, herds well fed and flourishing, stock multiplying abundantly— the supreme merit for pastoral officers;

sentences.zh: 二十七曰邊境清肅，城隍脩理，為鎮防之最。

translations.literal: twenty-seventh, frontier quiet and austere, walls and moats maintained, was the supreme merit for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-seventh, the border kept quiet and secure, walls and moats kept in repair— the supreme merit for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 一最四善為上上，一最三善為上中，一最二善為上下；

translations.literal: One supreme merit and four virtues made top-top; one supreme merit and three virtues made top-middle; one supreme merit and two virtues made top-bottom;
translations.idiomatic: One supreme merit plus four virtues rated top-top; one supreme merit plus three, top-middle; one supreme merit plus two, top-bottom;

sentences.zh: 無最而有二善為中上，無最而有一善為中中，職事粗理，善最不聞，為中下；

translations.literal: with no supreme merit but two virtues made middle-top; with no supreme merit but one virtue made middle-middle; duties roughly managed, neither virtue nor supreme merit noted, made middle-bottom;
translations.idiomatic: no supreme merit but two virtues, middle-top; no supreme merit but one virtue, middle-middle; duties only roughly managed, with no note of virtue or supreme merit, middle-bottom;

sentences.zh: 愛憎任情，處斷乖理，為下上；

translations.literal: love and hate at whim, judgments against reason, made bottom-top;
translations.idiomatic: partiality ruling judgment, decisions at odds with reason, bottom-top;

sentences.zh: 背公向私，職務廢闕，為下中；

translations.literal: turning from the public toward the private, official duties neglected and wanting, made bottom-middle;
translations.idiomatic: serving private ends over public duty, office left in neglect, bottom-middle;

sentences.zh: 居官諂詐，貪濁有狀，為下下。

translations.literal: in office given to flattery and fraud, greed and corruption with clear evidence, made bottom-bottom.
translations.idiomatic: flattery and deceit in office, greed and corruption plainly shown, bottom-bottom.

sentences.zh: 凡定考，皆集於尚書省，唱第然後奏。

translations.literal: In all, when finalizing examinations, all assembled at the Department of State Affairs; grades were announced aloud and then memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Final ratings were convened at the Department of State Affairs, announced in rank order, and then submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 親王及中書、門下、京官三品以上、都督、刺史、都護、節度、觀察使，則奏功過狀，以覈考行之上下。

translations.literal: For imperial princes and for officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery, capital officials of third rank and above, area commanders, prefects, protectors-general, military commissioners, and observation commissioners, records of merits and faults were memorialized to verify the high and low of conduct in examination.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, Secretariat and Chancellery officials, capital officers of third rank and above, area commanders, prefects, protectors-general, military commissioners, and observation commissioners submitted merit-and-fault records so the Examination Bureau could confirm their ratings.

sentences.zh: 每歲，尚書省諸司具州牧、刺史、縣令殊功異行，災蝗祥瑞，戶口賦役增減，盜賊多少，皆上於考司。

translations.literal: Each year the various offices of the Department of State Affairs compiled the special merits and unusual conduct of prefects, governors, and magistrates, disasters of locusts, auspicious omens, increases and decreases in households and tax corvée, and the number of bandits, all reporting upward to the Examination Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Each year every office under the Department of State Affairs forwarded to the Examination Bureau reports on prefects', governors', and magistrates' outstanding service, locust plagues and auspicious signs, changes in population and tax obligations, and levels of banditry.

sentences.zh: 監領之官，以能撫養役使者為功；

translations.literal: For supervising officials, ability to nurture corvée laborers counted as merit;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising officials were credited for keeping corvée workers well provisioned;

sentences.zh: 有耗亡者，以十分為率，一分為一殿。

translations.literal: where there was loss and depletion, taking ten parts as the measure, one part counted as one demerit.
translations.idiomatic: losses were measured in tenths, each tenth counting as one demerit mark.

sentences.zh: 博士、助教，計講授多少為差。

translations.literal: Erudites and assistant instructors were differentiated according to the amount of lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites and assistant instructors were graded by hours of instruction delivered.

sentences.zh: 親、勳、翊衞，以行能功過為三等，親、勳、翊衞備身，東宮親、勳、翊衞備身，王府執仗親事、執乘親事及親勳翊衞主帥、校尉、直長、品子、雜任、飛騎，皆上、中、下考，有二上第者，加階。

translations.literal: Personal Guard, Merit Guard, and Resplendent Guard were graded on conduct, ability, merit, and fault into three grades; Personal, Merit, and Resplendent Guard bodyguards, Eastern Palace Personal, Merit, and Resplendent Guard bodyguards, princely household weapon-bearing attendants and carriage attendants, and Personal-Merit-Resplendent Guard commanders, captains, duty chiefs, sons of ranked officials, miscellaneous appointees, and Flying Cavalry—all received upper, middle, or lower ratings; those with two top-tier ratings received added grade steps.
translations.idiomatic: Personal, Merit, and Resplendent Guards were rated upper, middle, or lower on conduct and performance; the same applied to their bodyguards, Eastern Palace and princely household guards, commanders, captains, duty chiefs, sons of ranked officials, miscellaneous appointees, and Flying Cavalry—and two top-tier ratings earned extra grade steps.

sentences.zh: 番考別為簿，以侍郎顓掌之。

translations.literal: Rotation examinations were kept in separate registers, exclusively managed by the vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Rotation-duty examinations were recorded in separate registers under the exclusive charge of the vice ministers.

sentences.zh: 流外官，以行能功過為四等：清謹勤公為上，執事無私為中，不勤其職為下，貪濁有狀為下下。

translations.literal: Flow-outside officials were graded on conduct, ability, merit, and fault into four grades: pure, careful, and diligent in public service rated upper; handling affairs without partiality rated middle; not diligent in office rated lower; greed and corruption with clear evidence rated bottom-bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Flow-outside officials fell into four grades: pure, careful public service earned upper; impartial execution of duty, middle; neglect of office, lower; proven greed and corruption, bottom-bottom.

sentences.zh: 凡考，中上以上，每進一等，加祿一季；

translations.literal: In all examinations, from middle-top upward, for each grade advanced, one season's salary was added;
translations.idiomatic: From middle-top upward, each grade above the norm added one season's salary;

sentences.zh: 中中，守本祿；

translations.literal: middle-middle kept the original salary;
translations.idiomatic: a middle-middle rating kept standard pay;

sentences.zh: 中下以下，每退一等，奪祿一季。

translations.literal: from middle-bottom downward, for each grade reduced, one season's salary was forfeited.
translations.idiomatic: from middle-bottom down, each grade below the norm cost one season's salary.

sentences.zh: 中品以下，四考皆中中者，進一階；

translations.literal: For middle rank and below, four examinations all middle-middle advanced one grade step;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of middle rank and below who earned middle-middle four times in a row advanced one grade step;

sentences.zh: 一中上考，復進一階；

translations.literal: one middle-top examination further advanced one grade step;
translations.idiomatic: one middle-top rating advanced another step;

sentences.zh: 一上下考，進二階；

translations.literal: one top-bottom examination advanced two grade steps;
translations.idiomatic: one top-bottom rating advanced two steps;

sentences.zh: 計當進而參有下考者，以一中上覆一中下，以一上下覆二中下。

translations.literal: When advancement was due but lower ratings were mixed in, one middle-top offset one middle-bottom, and one top-bottom offset two middle-bottom ratings.
translations.idiomatic: When promotion was otherwise due but lower ratings intervened, one middle-top cancelled one middle-bottom, and one top-bottom cancelled two middle-bottom marks.

sentences.zh: 上中以上，雖有下考，從上第。

translations.literal: From top-middle upward, even with lower ratings present, the higher rating prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: From top-middle up, a single lower mark did not drag down the overall standing.

sentences.zh: 有下下考者，解任。

translations.literal: Those with a bottom-bottom rating were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: A bottom-bottom rating meant removal from office.

sentences.zh: 凡制敕不便，有執奏者，進其考。

translations.literal: In all, where an edict or decree was inconvenient and someone remonstrated and memorialized, his examination was advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who remonstrated against impracticable edicts received a higher examination rating.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歲定京官望高者二人，分校京官、外官考，給事中、中書舍人各一人涖之，號監中外官考使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era, each year two capital officials of high standing were fixed to divide and grade capital and outer officials' examinations; one drafting attendant and one Secretariat drafter each oversaw them, titled Commissioners Overseeing Capital and Outer Examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, two senior capital officials were appointed annually to grade capital and provincial examinations separately, with one drafting attendant and one Secretariat drafter supervising— the Commissioners Overseeing Capital and Outer Examinations.

sentences.zh: 考功郎中判京官考，員外郎判外官考。

translations.literal: The director of the Bureau of Examination adjudicated capital examinations; the vice director adjudicated outer examinations.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Examination director handled capital ratings; the vice director, provincial ratings.

sentences.zh: 其後屢置監考、校考、知考使。

translations.literal: Thereafter overseers of examination, school examiners, and examination commissioners were repeatedly appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Later reigns repeatedly appointed overseers, school examiners, and examination commissioners.

sentences.zh: 故事，考簿朱書，吏緣為姦；

translations.literal: By precedent, examination registers were written in vermilion, and clerks exploited this for fraud;
translations.idiomatic: By old custom examination registers were kept in vermilion ink, which clerks turned to fraud;

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年，始以墨。

translations.literal: in the fourteenth year of Xiantong, black ink was first used.
translations.idiomatic: in 873 black ink was adopted instead.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue, one person, senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue had one minister of senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 侍郞二人，正四品下。

translations.literal: vice ministers, two persons, senior fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers of junior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌天下土地、人民、錢穀之政、貢賦之差。

translations.literal: They managed the policies of land, people, and grain throughout the realm, and the distinctions of tribute and taxation.
translations.idiomatic: They governed land, population, and grain policy empire-wide, and set the scales of tribute and taxation.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰戶部，二曰度支，三曰金部，四曰倉部。

translations.literal: Their subordinates were four: first Revenue, second Expenditure, third Treasury, fourth Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus reported to them: Revenue, Expenditure, Treasury, and Granaries.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中、員外郎，掌戶口、土田、賦役、貢獻、蠲免、優復、姻婚、繼嗣之事，以男女之黃、小、中、丁、老為之帳籍，以永業、口分、園宅均其土田，以租、庸、調斂其物，以九等定天下之戶，以為尚書、侍郎之貳。

translations.literal: Directors and vice directors of the Revenue Bureau managed households, land, tax corvée, tribute offerings, exemptions, preferential relief, marriage, and succession; they made registers according to yellow, minor, middle, adult, and elderly among men and women; they equalized land with permanent holdings, allotted fields, and garden homesteads; they collected goods through land tax, corvée, and the equalization tax; they fixed households throughout the realm in nine grades; and they assisted the minister and vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Bureau directors handled population registers, land, tax and corvée, tribute, exemptions, relief, marriage, and inheritance—classing men and women as infants, minors, adults, or elderly; apportioning permanent, allotted, and homestead land; collecting rent, corvée, and equalization dues; ranking households empire-wide in nine grades; and assisting the minister and vice ministers.

sentences.zh: 其後以諸行郎官判錢穀，而戶部、度支郎官失其職矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter directors from the various rows adjudicated finances, and the Revenue and Expenditure bureau directors lost their proper duties.
translations.idiomatic: Later, directors drawn from every ministry row took over fiscal adjudication, and the Revenue and Expenditure bureau directors were stripped of their proper charge.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年著令：以本行郎官，分判錢穀。

translations.literal: An ordinance issued in the second year of Huichang stipulated: directors of the home row were to divide and adjudicate finances.
translations.idiomatic: An ordinance of 842 restored the rule that home-row directors should divide fiscal adjudication among themselves.

sentences.zh: 戶部巡官二人，主事四人；

translations.literal: Revenue Bureau touring officials, two persons; section chiefs, four persons;
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Bureau had two touring officials and four section chiefs;

sentences.zh: 度支主事二人；

translations.literal: Expenditure Bureau section chiefs, two persons;
translations.idiomatic: the Expenditure Bureau, two section chiefs;

sentences.zh: 金部主事三人；

translations.literal: Treasury Bureau section chiefs, three persons;
translations.idiomatic: the Treasury Bureau, three section chiefs;

sentences.zh: 倉部主事三人。

translations.literal: Granaries Bureau section chiefs, three persons.
translations.idiomatic: the Granaries Bureau, three section chiefs.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，改民部曰戶部。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, the Ministry of Population was renamed Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozong's accession the Ministry of Population was renamed the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改戶部曰司元，度支曰司度，金部曰司珍，倉部曰司庾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, Revenue was renamed Directorate of Origins, Expenditure renamed Directorate of Measures, Treasury renamed Directorate of Treasures, and Granaries renamed Directorate of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 Revenue became the Directorate of Origins, Expenditure the Directorate of Measures, Treasury the Directorate of Treasures, and Granaries the Directorate of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，改戶部曰地官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, Revenue was renamed Earth Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 690 Revenue was renamed the Earth Office.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，改金部曰司金，倉部曰司儲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, Treasury was renamed Directorate of Metal, and Granaries renamed Directorate of Stores.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 Treasury became the Directorate of Metal and Granaries the Directorate of Stores.

sentences.zh: 有戶部令史十七人，書令史三十四人，計史一人，亭長六人，掌固十人；

translations.literal: There were seventeen Revenue Bureau clerks, thirty-four copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, six station chiefs, and ten custodians;
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Bureau employed seventeen clerks, thirty-four copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, six station chiefs, and ten custodians;

sentences.zh: 度支令史十六人，書令史三十三人，計史一人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Expenditure Bureau clerks sixteen, copy clerks thirty-three, reckoning clerk one, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: the Expenditure Bureau sixteen clerks, thirty-three copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 金部令史十人，書令史二十一人，計史一人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Treasury Bureau clerks ten, copy clerks twenty-one, reckoning clerk one, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: the Treasury Bureau ten clerks, twenty-one copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 倉部令史十二人，書令史二十三人，計史一人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Granaries Bureau clerks twelve, copy clerks twenty-three, reckoning clerk one, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: the Granaries Bureau twelve clerks, twenty-three copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 度支郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌天下租賦、物產豐約之宜、水陸道涂之利，歲計所出而支調之，以近及遠，與中書門下議定乃奏。

translations.literal: Expenditure Bureau director and vice director, one each, managed rent and levies throughout the realm, the suitability of abundant or scarce produce, and profits from land and water transport routes; they calculated yearly outlays and allocated disbursements from near to far, deliberated with the Secretariat-Chancellery, and then memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The Expenditure Bureau had one director and one vice director, charged with empire-wide rent and levies, the balance of plentiful and scarce produce, and the revenue of land and water routes. They reckoned annual expenditures, allocated funds from the center outward, settled matters with the Secretariat-Chancellery, and then submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 金部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌天下庫藏出納、權衡度量之數，兩京市、互市、和市、宮市交易之事，百官、軍鎮、蕃客之賜，及給宮人、王妃、官奴婢衣服。

translations.literal: Treasury Bureau director and vice director, one each, managed treasury receipts and disbursements throughout the realm and the standards of weights and measures; the markets of the two capitals, frontier trade, government purchase markets, and palace markets; grants to officials, garrisons, and foreign envoys; and the supply of clothing to palace women, imperial consorts, and official slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The Treasury Bureau had one director and one vice director, overseeing treasury inflow and outflow empire-wide, weights and measures, trade in the two capitals' markets, frontier exchange, government purchase markets, and palace markets, along with grants to officials, garrisons, and foreign guests, and clothing for palace women, consorts, and official bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌天下庫儲，出納租稅、祿糧、倉廩之事。

translations.literal: Granaries Bureau director and vice director, one each, managed granary stores throughout the realm and the receipt and disbursement of land tax, salary grain, and granary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Granaries Bureau had one director and one vice director, managing empire-wide storehouses and the intake and distribution of land tax, salary grain, and granary supplies.

sentences.zh: 以木契百，合諸司出給之數，以義倉、常平倉備凶年，平穀價。

translations.literal: One hundred wooden tallies recorded each office's disbursements; benevolence granaries and ever-normal granaries were kept against famine years to stabilize grain prices.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred wooden tally slips tracked each agency's disbursements; benevolence granaries and ever-normal granaries were maintained against bad harvests to stabilize grain prices.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Minister of Rites, one person, senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites had one minister of senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 侍郎一人，正四品下。

translations.literal: vice minister, one person, junior fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and one vice minister of junior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌禮儀、祭享、貢舉之政。

translations.literal: They managed the policies of ritual and etiquette, sacrificial offerings, and the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: They governed ritual and etiquette, sacrificial observances, and the civil examination system.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰禮部，二曰祠部，三曰膳部，四曰主客。

translations.literal: Under them were four bureaus: first the Bureau of Rites, second the Bureau of Sacrifices, third the Bureau of Provisions, fourth the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus reported to them: the Bureau of Rites, the Bureau of Sacrifices, the Bureau of Provisions, and the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中、員外郎，掌禮樂、學校、衣冠、符印、表疏、圖書、冊命、祥瑞、鋪設，及百官、宮人喪葬贈賻之數，為尚書、侍郎之貳。

translations.literal: The Rites Bureau director and vice director managed ritual music, schools, dress regulations, seals, memorials and petitions, books, investiture documents, auspicious omens, ceremonial furnishings, and the scales of funeral gifts for officials and palace personnel; they served as deputies to the minister and vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Bureau director and vice director oversaw ritual music, schools, dress codes, seals, memorials, books, investitures, auspicious omens, ceremonial arrangements, and funeral-gift scales for officials and palace staff, assisting the minister and vice minister.

sentences.zh: 五禮之儀：一曰吉禮，二曰賓禮，三曰軍禮，四曰嘉禮，五曰凶禮。

translations.literal: The five categories of ritual: first auspicious rites, second guest rites, third military rites, fourth felicitous rites, fifth mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The five ritual categories were auspicious rites, guest rites, military rites, felicitous rites, and mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 凡齊衰心喪以上奪情從職，及周喪未練、大功未葬，皆不預宴；

translations.literal: In general, those in first-degree hemp mourning or heart-mourning who had set grief aside to resume office, and those within the year of mourning not yet past the lian sacrifice or with close-relatives' mourning not yet buried, did not attend banquets.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, officials in first-degree mourning or heart-mourning who had been released from mourning to serve, and those still within the first year before the lian rite or with a close relative's funeral still unburied, did not join banquets.

sentences.zh: 大功以上喪，受冊涖官，鼓吹從而不作，戎事則否。

translations.literal: For mourning above the close-relatives' grade, when receiving appointment documents and assuming office, drums and pipes followed but did not sound; military duties excepted.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning above the close-relatives' degree, an appointee receiving his commission and taking office was escorted by drums and pipes that remained silent—except on military service.

sentences.zh: 凡朝，晚入、失儀，御史錄名奪俸，三奪者奏彈。

translations.literal: At court audiences, late arrival or breach of ceremony: the censor recorded names and docked salary; three dockings triggered a memorial of impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: At court, late arrival or breach of ritual earned a censor's notation and salary deduction; three deductions brought an impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 凡出蕃冊授、弔贈者，給衣冠。

translations.literal: In general, those sent abroad for investiture or condolence missions were supplied with ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys dispatched abroad for investiture or condolence were furnished with ceremonial robes.

sentences.zh: 皇帝巡幸，兩京文武官職事五品以上，月朔以表參起居；

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled, civil and military officials of the two capitals holding active posts of fifth rank and above submitted monthly memorials on the first of the month to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was on tour, active civil and military officials of fifth rank and above in both capitals sent monthly health-inquiry memorials on the first of each month.

sentences.zh: 近州刺史，遣使一參；

translations.literal: Prefects of nearby provinces dispatched envoys once to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby provincial prefects sent envoys once to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 留守，月遣使起居；

translations.literal: Caretaker commissioners monthly dispatched envoys to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: Capital caretakers sent monthly envoys to inquire after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 北都，則四時遣使起居。

translations.literal: For the Northern Capital, envoys were dispatched at the four seasons to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: For the Northern Capital, seasonal envoys were sent four times a year to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 諸司奏大事者，前期三日具狀，長官躬署，對仗伏奏，仗下，中書門下涖讀。

translations.literal: Offices memorializing major matters submitted written petitions three days in advance, personally signed by the chief; they kneeled to present before the imperial guard; after the guard withdrew, the Secretariat-Chancellery read them.
translations.idiomatic: Agencies reporting major business filed written petitions three days ahead, signed by the chief in person; they knelt to present before the imperial guard, and after the guard withdrew the Secretariat-Chancellery read the memorial aloud.

sentences.zh: 河南、太原府父老，每歲上表願駕幸，遣使以聞。

translations.literal: Elder worthies of Henan and Taiyuan prefectures annually submitted memorials inviting an imperial visit, dispatching envoys to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Each year elders of Henan and Taiyuan prefectures submitted memorials inviting the emperor to visit, sending envoys to announce their wish.

sentences.zh: 駕在都，則京兆府亦如之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the capital, Jingzhao Prefecture did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor resided in the capital, Jingzhao Prefecture followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 凡景雲、慶雲為大瑞，其名物六十有四；

translations.literal: Luminous clouds and celebratory clouds counted as great omens, with sixty-four named manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: Luminous and celebratory clouds ranked as great omens, with sixty-four recognized forms.

sentences.zh: 白狼、赤兔為上瑞，其名物三十有八；

translations.literal: White wolves and red hares counted as supreme omens, with thirty-eight named manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: White wolves and red hares ranked as supreme omens, with thirty-eight recognized forms.

sentences.zh: 蒼烏、朱雁為中瑞，其名物三十有二；

translations.literal: Dark birds and vermilion geese counted as middling omens, with thirty-two named manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: Dark birds and vermilion geese ranked as middling omens, with thirty-two recognized forms.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾、芝草、木連理為下瑞，其名物十四。

translations.literal: Fine grain, spirit fungus, and trees with conjoined trunks counted as lesser omens, with fourteen named manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: Fine grain, spirit fungus, and conjoined trees ranked as lesser omens, with fourteen recognized forms.

sentences.zh: 大瑞，則百官詣闕奉賀；

translations.literal: For great omens, all officials went to the palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Upon a great omen, officials throughout the court went to the palace to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 餘瑞，歲終員外郎以聞，有司告廟。

translations.literal: For other omens, at year's end the vice director reported, and the proper office notified the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser omens were reported by the vice director at year's end, and the responsible office announced them at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 凡喪，三品以上稱薨，五品以上稱卒，自六品達于庶人稱死。

translations.literal: For deaths: third rank and above were termed "passed away," fifth rank and above "deceased," and from sixth rank down to commoners "died."
translations.idiomatic: Death terminology ran by rank: third rank and above were said to have "passed away," fifth rank and above to have "deceased," and sixth rank down to commoners simply to have "died."

sentences.zh: 皇親三等以上喪，舉哀，有司帳具給食；

translations.literal: For mourning among imperial relatives of third degree and above, lamentation was raised and the proper office set up tents and supplied food.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial kin of the third degree or closer mourned, public lament was raised and the responsible office pitched tents and provided meals.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃首領喪，則主客、鴻臚月奏。

translations.literal: For mourning among foreign chieftains, the Bureau of Receptions and the Court of Imperial Entertainments submitted monthly reports.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign chieftains died, the Bureau of Receptions and the Court of Imperial Entertainments filed monthly reports.

sentences.zh: 禮部主事二人，祠部主事二人，膳部主事二人，主客主事二人。

translations.literal: Rites Bureau section chiefs, two persons; Sacrifices Bureau section chiefs, two persons; Provisions Bureau section chiefs, two persons; Receptions Bureau section chiefs, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Bureau had two section chiefs, the Sacrifices Bureau two, the Provisions Bureau two, and the Receptions Bureau two.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，改儀曹郎曰禮部郎中，司藩郎曰主客郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, the Protocol Bureau director was renamed Rites Bureau director, and the Foreign Affairs Bureau director was renamed Receptions Bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 the Protocol Bureau director became the Rites Bureau director, and the Foreign Affairs Bureau director became the Receptions Bureau director.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改禮部曰司禮，祠部曰司禋，膳部曰司膳，光宅元年，改禮部曰春官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, Rites was renamed Directorate of Rites, Sacrifices renamed Directorate of Sacrifice, Provisions renamed Directorate of Provisions; in the first year of Guangzhai, Rites was renamed Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 Rites became the Directorate of Rites, Sacrifices the Directorate of Sacrifice, and Provisions the Directorate of Provisions; in 690 Rites was renamed the Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 有禮部令史五人，書令史十一人，亭長六人，掌固八人；

translations.literal: Rites Bureau clerks five, copy clerks eleven, station chiefs six, custodians eight;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites Bureau had five clerks, eleven copy clerks, six station chiefs, and eight custodians;

sentences.zh: 祠部令史六人，書令史十三人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Sacrifices Bureau clerks six, copy clerks thirteen, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: the Sacrifices Bureau six clerks, thirteen copy clerks, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 主客令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Receptions Bureau clerks four, copy clerks nine, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: the Receptions Bureau four clerks, nine copy clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌祠祀、享祭、天文、漏刻、國忌、廟諱、卜筮、醫藥、僧尼之事。

translations.literal: Sacrifices Bureau director and vice director, one each, managed sacrifices and offerings, astronomy, clepsydra water clocks, national days of mourning, taboo names in temples, divination, medicine, and Buddhist and Daoist monastics.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrifices Bureau had one director and one vice director, overseeing sacrifices and offerings, astronomy, water clocks, national mourning days, temple taboo names, divination, medicine, and Buddhist and Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 珠玉珍寶供祭者，不求於市。

translations.literal: Pearls, jade, and precious things for sacrifice were not sought in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls, jade, and other precious offerings for sacrifice were not purchased in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 駕部、比部歲會牲之死亡，輸皮於太府。

translations.literal: The Bureaus of Transport and Review annually tallied sacrificial animals that died and delivered hides to the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Transport and Review bureaus accounted for sacrificial livestock that died and sent the hides to the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 郊祭酒醴、脯醢、黍稷、果實，所司長官封署以供。

translations.literal: For suburban sacrifices, wine, dried and pickled meats, millet, and fruit—the responsible chief sealed and signed them for supply.
translations.idiomatic: Wine, dried and pickled meats, millet, and fruit for suburban sacrifices were sealed and signed by the responsible chief before delivery.

sentences.zh: 兩京及磧西諸州火祆，歲再祀，而禁民祈祭。

translations.literal: In the two capitals and Qiuxi prefectures, Zoroastrian fire temples were worshipped twice yearly, while popular prayer sacrifices were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In both capitals and the western desert prefectures, Zoroastrian fire temples received worship twice a year, while private prayer sacrifices by the people were prohibited.

sentences.zh: 凡巡幸，路次名山、大川、聖帝明王名臣墓，州縣以官告祭。

translations.literal: On imperial tours, famous mountains, great rivers, and tombs of sage emperors, enlightened kings, and eminent ministers along the route were announced and sacrificed to by prefectures and counties with official rites.
translations.idiomatic: During imperial progress, prefectures and counties along the route performed official announcement and sacrifice at famous mountains, great rivers, and the tombs of sage emperors, enlightened kings, and renowned ministers.

sentences.zh: 二王後享廟，則給牲牢、祭器，而完其帷帟、几案，主客以四時省問。

translations.literal: When descendants of the two earlier dynasties performed ancestral temple rites, sacrificial animals and vessels were supplied, and their curtains, screens, tables, and stands were maintained; the Bureau of Receptions inspected seasonally.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Founders' descendants held temple rites, they received sacrificial livestock and vessels, their curtains, screens, tables, and stands were kept in repair, and the Bureau of Receptions conducted seasonal inspections.

sentences.zh: 凡國忌廢務日，內教、太常停習樂，兩京文武五品以上及清官七品以上，行香於寺觀。

translations.literal: On national mourning days when business was suspended, the Inner Conservatory and Court of Imperial Sacrifices halted musical practice; capital civil and military officials of fifth rank and above and pure officials of seventh rank and above burned incense at temples and monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: On national mourning days when offices stood idle, the Inner Conservatory and Court of Imperial Sacrifices ceased musical rehearsal; capital civil and military officials of fifth rank and above, and pure officials of seventh rank and above, burned incense at temples and monasteries.

sentences.zh: 凡名醫子弟試療病，長官涖覆，三年有驗者以名聞。

translations.literal: Distinguished physicians' students were tested in treating illness under the chief's supervision; after three years those with verified success were reported by name.
translations.idiomatic: Students of renowned physicians were tested in clinical treatment under supervisory review; after three years those whose skill was proven were reported by name.

sentences.zh: 膳部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌陵廟之牲豆酒膳。

translations.literal: Provisions Bureau director and vice director, one each, managed sacrificial animals, vessels, wine, and food for imperial tombs and ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Provisions Bureau had one director and one vice director, charged with sacrificial livestock, vessels, wine, and food for imperial tombs and ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 諸司供奉口味，躬鐍其輿乃遣，進胙亦如之。

translations.literal: Tribute delicacies from various offices: the chief personally sealed the transport carts before dispatch; presentation of sacrificial flesh likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Delicacies submitted by various offices had to be personally sealed by the chief before the carts were sent; presentation of sacrificial meat followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 非大禮、大慶不獻食，不進口味。

translations.literal: Except for grand rites or grand celebrations, food was not offered and delicacies were not presented.
translations.idiomatic: Food offerings and delicacies were presented only at major rites or major celebrations.

sentences.zh: 凡羊，至廚而乳者釋之長生。

translations.literal: In general, ewes that had lambed upon reaching the kitchen were released for long life.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, ewes that had given birth by the time they reached the kitchen were released alive as an act of mercy.

sentences.zh: 大齋日，尚食進蔬食，釋所殺羊為長生供奉。

translations.literal: On great fast days, the Imperial Kitchen served vegetarian food and released slaughtered sheep as long-life offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On great fast days the Imperial Kitchen served vegetarian fare and released sheep slated for slaughter as long-life offerings.

sentences.zh: 凡獻食、進口味，不殺犢。

translations.literal: For food offerings and delicacies, calves were not slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Calves were not killed for food offerings or delicacies.

sentences.zh: 尚食有猝須別索，必奏覆，月終而會之。

translations.literal: If the Imperial Kitchen had sudden special requisitions, memorial approval was required, with monthly accounting at month's end.
translations.idiomatic: Emergency special requisitions by the Imperial Kitchen required memorial approval and were reconciled in a monthly account at month's end.

sentences.zh: 凡尚食進食，以種取而別嘗之。

translations.literal: For imperial food service, samples were taken by type and tasted separately.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial meals were tested by taking a sample of each kind and tasting it separately.

sentences.zh: 殿中省主膳上食於諸陵，以番上下，四時遣食醫、主食各一人涖之。

translations.literal: The Palace Domestic Service's provision stewards served food at the various tombs in rotating shifts; each season one food physician and one chief provisioner were dispatched to oversee.
translations.idiomatic: Palace provision stewards served food at the imperial tombs in rotation; each season one food physician and one chief provisioner were sent to supervise.

sentences.zh: 主客郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌二王後、諸蕃朝見之事。

translations.literal: Receptions Bureau director and vice director, one each, managed the two founders' descendants and all foreign peoples' court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The Receptions Bureau had one director and one vice director, handling the Two Founders' descendants and court audiences by foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 二王後子孫視正三品，酅公歲賜絹三百，米粟亦如之，介公減三之一。

translations.literal: Descendants of the two earlier dynasties were treated as senior third rank; the Duke of Xi annually received three hundred bolts of silk and the same measure of grain, the Duke of Jie one-third less.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Founders' descendants were accorded senior third rank; the Duke of Xi received three hundred bolts of silk annually and the same quantity of grain, the Duke of Jie one-third less.

sentences.zh: 殊俗入朝者，始至之州給牒，覆其人數，謂之邊牒。

translations.literal: Foreign envoys entering court received travel documents at their first-arrival province; their numbers were verified—these were called frontier travel slips.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys bound for court received travel documents at the first province they entered; their numbers were checked—these were called frontier travel slips.

sentences.zh: 蕃州都督、刺史朝集日，視品給以衣冠、袴褶。

translations.literal: On the annual assembly day for frontier prefecture protectors and prefects, ceremonial dress and military-style tunics were granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the annual assembly, frontier protectors and prefects received ceremonial robes and riding dress according to rank.

sentences.zh: 乘傳者日四驛，乘驛者六驛。

translations.literal: Those traveling by official courier post covered four relay stations per day; those by standard post, six relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers on urgent courier post covered four relay stages per day; those on regular post, six.

sentences.zh: 供客食料，以四時輸鴻臚，季終句會之。

translations.literal: Guest provisions were delivered to the Court of Imperial Entertainments each season and reconciled at quarter's end.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions for guests were forwarded to the Court of Imperial Entertainments each season and audited at quarter's end.

sentences.zh: 客初至及辭設會，第一等視三品，第二等視四品，第三等視五品，蕃望非高者，視散官而減半，參日設食。

translations.literal: For envoys on arrival and farewell banquets: first rank treated as third rank, second as fourth, third as fifth; those of lesser tribal standing treated as honorary rank but halved; banquets set on the day of attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Arrival and farewell banquets ranked guests as follows: first class as third rank, second as fourth, third as fifth; envoys of lesser standing were treated at half the scale of their honorary rank; banquets were held on the day of attendance.

sentences.zh: 路由大海者，給祈羊豕皆一。

translations.literal: Routes crossing the great sea received one sheep and one pig each for prayer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers on routes crossing the open sea were supplied one sheep and one pig each for prayer sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 西南蕃使還者，給入海程糧；

translations.literal: Southwestern envoys returning were given provisions for the sea voyage.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern envoys returning home received rations for the sea crossing.

sentences.zh: 西北諸蕃，則給度磧程糧。

translations.literal: Northwestern peoples received provisions for crossing the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern envoys received rations for crossing the desert.

sentences.zh: 蕃客請宿衞者，奏狀貌年齒。

translations.literal: Foreign guests requesting palace guard duty memorialized their appearance and age.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests who sought palace guard service submitted memorials describing their appearance and age.

sentences.zh: 突厥使置市坊，有貿易，錄奏，為質其輕重，太府丞一人涖之。

translations.literal: Turkish envoys were assigned market wards; when trade occurred it was recorded and reported, goods weighed for quality, with one vice director of the Imperial Storehouse supervising.
translations.idiomatic: Turkish envoys were lodged in designated market wards; trade was logged and reported, goods weighed to establish value, under supervision of an Imperial Storehouse vice director.

sentences.zh: 蕃王首領死，子孫襲初授官，兄弟子降一品，兄弟子代攝者，嫡年十五還以政。

translations.literal: When foreign kings or chieftains died, descendants inherited their initial conferred rank; brothers' sons dropped one rank; when a brother's son served as regent, when the heir reached fifteen the government was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign kings or chieftains died, sons inherited the originally conferred rank; a brother's son dropped one rank; if a brother's son served as regent, authority reverted to the heir at age fifteen.

sentences.zh: 使絕域者還，上聞見及風俗之宜、供饋贈貺之數。

translations.literal: Envoys returning from distant regions reported what they had seen and heard, local customs, and the scale of provisions and gifts exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys back from distant lands submitted reports on what they had seen and heard, local customs, and the quantities of provisions and gifts exchanged.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Minister of War, one person, senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War had one minister of senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 侍郞二人，正四品下。

translations.literal: vice ministers, two persons, junior fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and two vice ministers of junior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌武選、地圖、車馬、甲械之政。

translations.literal: They managed the policies of military appointments, maps, chariots and horses, and armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: They governed military appointments, maps, chariots and horses, and armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰兵部，二曰職方，三曰駕部，四曰庫部。

translations.literal: Under them were four bureaus: first the War Bureau, second the Bureau of Operations, third the Bureau of Transport, fourth the Bureau of Armory.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus reported to them: the War Bureau, the Bureau of Operations, the Bureau of Transport, and the Bureau of Armory.

sentences.zh: 凡將出征，告廟，授斧鉞；

translations.literal: When generals marched, the ancestral temple was notified and battle-axes were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Before a general took the field, the ancestral temple was notified and battle-axes were conferred upon him.

sentences.zh: 軍不從令，大將專決，還日，具上其罪。

translations.literal: If troops disobeyed orders, the commander decided alone; on return, the offenses were fully reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: When troops disobeyed orders, the commanding general decided punishment on his own authority; on return he submitted a full report of their offenses.

sentences.zh: 凡發兵，降敕書於尚書，尚書下文符。

translations.literal: To mobilize troops, an edict was issued to the minister, who dispatched written orders.
translations.idiomatic: Troop mobilization began with an edict to the minister, who then issued written orders.

sentences.zh: 放十人，發十馬，軍器出十，皆不待敕。

translations.literal: Deployments of ten men, ten horses, or ten weapons of war did not require an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatching ten men, ten horses, or ten pieces of military equipment did not require an edict.

sentences.zh: 衞士番直；

translations.literal: Guard soldiers rotated duty.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards served in rotating shifts.

sentences.zh: 發一人以上，必覆奏。

translations.literal: Dispatch of one or more required memorial approval.
translations.idiomatic: Sending even a single man required a memorial for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃首領至，則備威儀郊導。

translations.literal: When foreign chieftains arrived, full ceremonial guard met them in suburban welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign chieftains arrived, full ceremonial escort went out to the suburbs to receive them.

sentences.zh: 凡俘馘，酬以絹，入鈔之俘，歸於司農。

translations.literal: Captives and severed heads were rewarded with silk; captives registered on tally slips went to the Court of the National Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Captives and severed heads earned silk rewards; captives entered on tally registers were turned over to the Court of the National Granaries.

sentences.zh: 郎中一人判帳及武官階品、衞府眾寡、校考、給告身之事；

translations.literal: One director adjudicated registers and military ranks and grades, guard strength, examination review, and the issuance of commission certificates.
translations.idiomatic: One director handled registers, military ranks and grades, guard-house strength, performance review, and commission certificates.

sentences.zh: 一人判簿及軍戎調遣之名數，朝集、祿賜、假告之常。

translations.literal: One director adjudicated ledgers and the numbers for military dispatch, annual assembly, salary grants, and routine leave.
translations.idiomatic: One director managed ledgers, troop dispatch figures, annual assembly, salary grants, and routine leave.

sentences.zh: 員外郎一人掌貢舉、雜請；

translations.literal: One vice director managed the examinations and miscellaneous petitions.
translations.idiomatic: One vice director oversaw examinations and miscellaneous petitions.

sentences.zh: 一人判南曹，歲選解狀，則覈簿書、資歷、考課。

translations.literal: One director adjudicated the Southern Registry; when annual selection dossiers were submitted, he verified ledgers, credentials, and performance ratings.
translations.idiomatic: One director handled the Southern Registry; at annual selection he checked ledgers, credentials, and performance ratings.

sentences.zh: 皆為尚書、侍郎之貳。

translations.literal: All served as deputies to the minister and vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: All assisted the minister and vice ministers.

sentences.zh: 武散階四十有五：從一品曰驃騎大將軍；

translations.literal: Military honorary ranks numbered forty-five: junior first rank was Grand General of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: There were forty-five military honorary ranks; junior first rank was Grand General of Fast Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 正二品曰輔國大將軍；

translations.literal: Senior second rank was Grand General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Senior second rank was Grand General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 從二品曰鎮軍大將軍；

translations.literal: Junior second rank was Grand General Who Suppresses Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Junior second rank was Grand General Who Suppresses Armies.

sentences.zh: 正三品上曰冠軍大將軍、懷化大將軍；

translations.literal: Senior third rank, upper grade: Grand General Who Crowns the Army and Grand General Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Senior third rank, upper grade: Grand General Who Crowns the Army and Grand General Who Cherishes Transformation.

sentences.zh: 正三品下曰懷化將軍；

translations.literal: Senior third rank, lower grade: General Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Senior third rank, lower grade: General Who Cherishes Transformation.

sentences.zh: 從三品上曰雲麾將軍、歸德大將軍；

translations.literal: Junior third rank, upper grade: General of Cloud Pennons and Grand General Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Junior third rank, upper grade: General of Cloud Pennons and Grand General Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 從三品下曰歸德將軍；

translations.literal: Junior third rank, lower grade: General Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Junior third rank, lower grade: General Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 正四品上曰忠武將軍；

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank, upper grade: General of Loyal Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, upper grade: General of Loyal Martiality.

sentences.zh: 正四品下曰壯武將軍、懷化中郎將；

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank, lower grade: General of Robust Martiality and Palace Guard General Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, lower grade: General of Robust Martiality and Palace Guard General Who Cherishes Transformation.

sentences.zh: 從四品上曰宣威將軍；

translations.literal: Junior fourth rank, upper grade: General Who Proclaims Might.
translations.idiomatic: Junior fourth rank, upper grade: General Who Proclaims Might.

sentences.zh: 從四品下曰明威將軍、歸德中郎將；

translations.literal: Junior fourth rank, lower grade: General of Bright Might and Palace Guard General Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Junior fourth rank, lower grade: General of Bright Might and Palace Guard General Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 正五品上曰定遠將軍；

translations.literal: Senior fifth rank, upper grade: General Who Secures the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fifth rank, upper grade: General Who Secures the Distance.

sentences.zh: 正五品下曰寧遠將軍、懷化郎將；

translations.literal: Senior fifth rank, lower grade: General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commandant Who Cherishes Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fifth rank, lower grade: General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commandant Who Cherishes Transformation.

sentences.zh: 從五品上曰游騎將軍；

translations.literal: Junior fifth rank, upper grade: General of the Roaming Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Junior fifth rank, upper grade: General of the Roaming Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從五品下曰游擊將軍、歸德郎將；

translations.literal: Junior fifth rank, lower grade: General of the Roaming Attack and Commandant Who Returns to Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Junior fifth rank, lower grade: General of the Roaming Attack and Commandant Who Returns to Virtue.

sentences.zh: 正六品上曰昭武校尉；

translations.literal: Senior sixth rank, upper grade was titled Captain of Manifest Martiality;
translations.idiomatic: Senior sixth rank, upper grade, bore the title Captain of Manifest Martiality;

sentences.zh: 正六品下曰昭武副尉、懷化司階；

translations.literal: senior sixth rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain of Manifest Martiality and Squire of Pacifying Transformation;
translations.idiomatic: senior sixth rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain of Manifest Martiality and Squire of Pacifying Transformation;

sentences.zh: 從六品上曰振威校尉；

translations.literal: junior sixth rank, upper grade was titled Captain of Quelling Might;
translations.idiomatic: junior sixth rank, upper grade, Captain of Quelling Might;

sentences.zh: 從六品下曰振威副尉、歸德司階；

translations.literal: junior sixth rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain of Quelling Might and Squire of Returning Virtue;
translations.idiomatic: junior sixth rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain of Quelling Might and Squire of Returning Virtue;

sentences.zh: 正七品上曰致果校尉；

translations.literal: senior seventh rank, upper grade was titled Captain of Attaining Merit;
translations.idiomatic: senior seventh rank, upper grade, Captain of Attaining Merit;

sentences.zh: 正七品下曰致果副尉、懷化中候；

translations.literal: senior seventh rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain of Attaining Merit and Warden of Pacifying Transformation;
translations.idiomatic: senior seventh rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain of Attaining Merit and Warden of Pacifying Transformation;

sentences.zh: 從七品上曰翊麾校尉；

translations.literal: junior seventh rank, upper grade was titled Captain Who Assists the Standard;
translations.idiomatic: junior seventh rank, upper grade, Captain Who Assists the Standard;

sentences.zh: 從七品下曰翊麾副尉、歸德中候；

translations.literal: junior seventh rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain Who Assists the Standard and Warden of Returning Virtue;
translations.idiomatic: junior seventh rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain Who Assists the Standard and Warden of Returning Virtue;

sentences.zh: 正八品上曰宣節校尉；

translations.literal: senior eighth rank, upper grade was titled Captain Who Proclaims Integrity;
translations.idiomatic: senior eighth rank, upper grade, Captain Who Proclaims Integrity;

sentences.zh: 正八品下曰宣節副尉、懷化司戈；

translations.literal: senior eighth rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain Who Proclaims Integrity and Spear-Bearer of Pacifying Transformation;
translations.idiomatic: senior eighth rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain Who Proclaims Integrity and Spear-Bearer of Pacifying Transformation;

sentences.zh: 從八品上曰禦侮校尉；

translations.literal: junior eighth rank, upper grade was titled Captain Who Repels Insult;
translations.idiomatic: junior eighth rank, upper grade, Captain Who Repels Insult;

sentences.zh: 從八品下曰禦侮副尉、歸德司戈；

translations.literal: junior eighth rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain Who Repels Insult and Spear-Bearer of Returning Virtue;
translations.idiomatic: junior eighth rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain Who Repels Insult and Spear-Bearer of Returning Virtue;

sentences.zh: 正九品上曰仁勇校尉；

translations.literal: senior ninth rank, upper grade was titled Captain of Humane Courage;
translations.idiomatic: senior ninth rank, upper grade, Captain of Humane Courage;

sentences.zh: 正九品下曰仁勇副尉、懷化執戟長上；

translations.literal: senior ninth rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain of Humane Courage and Long-Service Halberd Bearer of Pacifying Transformation;
translations.idiomatic: senior ninth rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain of Humane Courage and Long-Service Halberd Bearer of Pacifying Transformation;

sentences.zh: 從九品上曰陪戎校尉；

translations.literal: junior ninth rank, upper grade was titled Captain Attending the Host;
translations.idiomatic: junior ninth rank, upper grade, Captain Attending the Host;

sentences.zh: 從九品下曰陪戎副尉、歸德執戟長上。

translations.literal: junior ninth rank, lower grade was titled Deputy Captain Attending the Host and Long-Service Halberd Bearer of Returning Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: junior ninth rank, lower grade, Deputy Captain Attending the Host and Long-Service Halberd Bearer of Returning Virtue.

sentences.zh: 自四品以下，皆番上於兵部，以遠近為八番，三月一上；

translations.literal: From fourth rank downward, all reported in rotation at the Ministry of War; by distance they were divided into eight rotations, one rotation every three months;
translations.idiomatic: From fourth rank down, all reported for rotating duty at the Ministry of War, apportioned into eight shifts by distance, each shift lasting three months;

sentences.zh: 三千里外者免番，輸資如文散官，唯追集乃上。

translations.literal: those three thousand li or more abroad were exempt from rotation, paid capital-residence fees like civil prestige-rank holders, and reported only when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: those posted three thousand li or more from the capital were exempt from rotation, paid capital-residence fees like civil prestige-rank holders, and reported only when called up.

sentences.zh: 六品以下，尚書省送符。

translations.literal: For sixth rank and below, the Department of State Affairs sent tally slips.
translations.idiomatic: For sixth rank and below, the Department of State Affairs issued dispatch tallies.

sentences.zh: 懷化大將軍、歸德大將軍，配諸衞上下；

translations.literal: Generals of Pacifying Transformation and Generals of Returning Virtue were assigned to upper and lower ranks in the various Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Generals of Pacifying Transformation and Generals of Returning Virtue were posted to upper and lower slots in the various Guards;

sentences.zh: 餘直諸衞為十二番，皆月上。

translations.literal: the remainder on direct duty with the various Guards formed twelve rotations, all reporting monthly.
translations.idiomatic: the rest on direct palace-guard duty with the various Guards formed twelve monthly rotations.

sentences.zh: 忠武將軍以下、游擊將軍以上，每番，閱彊毅者直諸衞；

translations.literal: From Loyal Martial General down through Raider General up, each rotation selected the strongest and most resolute for direct duty with the Guards;
translations.idiomatic: From Loyal Martial General down to Raider General up, each rotation picked the strongest and most resolute for direct guard duty;

sentences.zh: 番滿，有將略者以名聞。

translations.literal: when a rotation term was complete, those with military talent were reported by name.
translations.idiomatic: when a rotation term ended, men of proven martial talent were reported by name.

sentences.zh: 兵部主事四人，職方主事二人，駕部主事二人，庫部主事二人。

translations.literal: Ministry of War section chiefs four, Border Affairs section chiefs two, Transport section chiefs two, Armories section chiefs two.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War had four section chiefs, Border Affairs two, Transport two, and Armories two.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改兵部曰司戎，職方曰司城，駕部曰司輿，庫部曰司庫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, War was renamed Directorate of Armies, Border Affairs renamed Directorate of Fortifications, Transport renamed Directorate of Carriages, Armories renamed Directorate of Stores.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 the ministry became the Directorate of Armies, Border Affairs the Directorate of Fortifications, Transport the Directorate of Carriages, and Armories the Directorate of Stores.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，改兵部曰夏官，天寶十一載曰武部，駕部曰司駕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, War was renamed Summer Office; in the eleventh year of Tianbao, War was renamed Military Department, and Transport renamed Directorate of Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 War was renamed the Summer Office; in 752 it became the Military Department, and Transport the Directorate of Carriage.

sentences.zh: 有兵部令史三十人，書令史六十人，制書令史十三人，甲庫令史十二人，亭長八人，掌固十二人；

translations.literal: There were thirty Ministry of War clerks, sixty copy clerks, thirteen edict clerks, twelve armor-archive clerks, eight station chiefs, and twelve custodians;
translations.idiomatic: The ministry employed thirty clerks, sixty copy clerks, thirteen edict clerks, twelve armor-archive clerks, eight station chiefs, and twelve custodians;

sentences.zh: 職方令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Border Affairs clerks four, copy clerks nine, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: Border Affairs four clerks, nine copy clerks, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 駕部令史十人，書令史二十四人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Transport clerks ten, copy clerks twenty-four, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: Transport ten clerks, twenty-four copy clerks, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 庫部令史七人，書令史十五人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Armories clerks seven, copy clerks fifteen, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Armories seven clerks, fifteen copy clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 職方郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌地圖、城隍、鎮戍、烽候、防人道路之遠近及四夷歸化之事。

translations.literal: Border Affairs directors and vice directors, one each, managed maps, walled cities, garrison posts, beacon towers, frontier personnel, the distances of roads, and the submission of the four directions' barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Border Affairs had one director and one vice director, charged with maps, walled cities, garrison posts, beacon towers, frontier personnel, road distances, and the submission of foreign peoples from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 凡圖經，非州縣增廢，五年乃脩，歲與版籍偕上。

translations.literal: In all, gazetteers, unless prefectures or counties were abolished or created, were revised every five years and submitted annually with household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Gazetteers were revised every five years unless a prefecture or county was abolished or created, and submitted each year together with household registers.

sentences.zh: 凡蕃客至，鴻臚訊其國山川、風土，為圖奏之，副上於職方；

translations.literal: When foreign guests arrived, the Court of State Ceremonial inquired about their country's mountains, rivers, and customs, made a map and submitted it, and sent a duplicate to Border Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys arrived, the Court of State Ceremonial questioned them on their homeland's mountains, rivers, and customs, drew a map for submission, and forwarded a copy to Border Affairs;

sentences.zh: 殊俗入朝者，圖其容狀、衣服以聞。

translations.literal: foreigners coming to court had their appearance and dress diagrammed and reported.
translations.idiomatic: foreigners presenting themselves at court had their features and dress sketched and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 駕部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌輿輦、車乘、傳驛、廄牧馬牛雜畜之籍。

translations.literal: Transport directors and vice directors, one each, managed the registers of imperial carriages, vehicles, relay posts, and stables for horses, cattle, and miscellaneous livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Transport had one director and one vice director, who kept registers of imperial carriages, vehicles, relay stations, and stable herds of horses, cattle, and other livestock.

sentences.zh: 凡給馬者，一品八匹，二品六匹，三品五匹，四品、五品四匹，六品三匹，七品以下二匹；

translations.literal: In all, for issuing horses: first rank eight, second rank six, third rank five, fourth and fifth ranks four, sixth rank three, seventh rank and below two;
translations.idiomatic: Horses were allotted by rank: eight for first rank, six for second, five for third, four for fourth and fifth, three for sixth, and two for seventh rank and below;

sentences.zh: 給傳乘者，一品十馬，二品九馬，三品八馬，四品、五品四馬，六品、七品二馬，八品、九品一馬；

translations.literal: for issuing relay transport: first rank ten horses, second rank nine, third rank eight, fourth and fifth ranks four, sixth and seventh ranks two, eighth and ninth ranks one;
translations.idiomatic: relay mounts ran ten horses for first rank, nine for second, eight for third, four for fourth and fifth, two for sixth and seventh, and one for eighth and ninth;

sentences.zh: 三品以上敕召者給四馬，五品三馬，六品以下有差。

translations.literal: those of third rank and above summoned by imperial edict received four horses; fifth rank three horses; sixth rank and below with graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: third rank and above, when summoned by edict, received four horses; fifth rank, three; sixth rank and below, graded allotments.

sentences.zh: 凡驛馬，給地四頃，蒔以苜蓿。

translations.literal: In all, relay horses were granted four qing of land, planted with alfalfa.
translations.idiomatic: Each relay horse was granted four qing of land sown with alfalfa.

sentences.zh: 凡三十里有驛，驛有長，舉天下四方之所達，為驛千六百三十九；

translations.literal: In all, every thirty li there was a post; each post had a chief; counting every route reachable throughout the realm under the four directions, there were one thousand six hundred thirty-nine posts;
translations.idiomatic: Every thirty li marked a relay post, each with its chief; routes reaching every quarter of the empire totaled one thousand six hundred thirty-nine posts;

sentences.zh: 阻險無水草鎮戍者，視路要隙置官馬。

translations.literal: where terrain was hazardous and garrison posts lacked water and fodder, official horses were placed at strategic points along the route.
translations.idiomatic: where terrain was treacherous and garrison posts lacked water and fodder, government horses were posted at key points along the line.

sentences.zh: 水驛有舟。

translations.literal: Water relay posts had boats.
translations.idiomatic: River relay stations maintained boats.

sentences.zh: 凡傳驛馬驢，每歲上其死損、肥瘠之數。

translations.literal: In all, relay horses and donkeys each year reported upward the numbers dead, lost, fat, and lean.
translations.idiomatic: Each year relay horses and donkeys reported deaths, losses, and counts of fat and lean stock.

sentences.zh: 庫部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌戎器、鹵簿儀仗。

translations.literal: Armories directors and vice directors, one each, managed weapons and ceremonial guard regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Armories had one director and one vice director, charged with weapons and ceremonial guard regalia.

sentences.zh: 元日冬至陳設、祠祀、喪葬，辨其名數而供焉。

translations.literal: New Year's Day and Winter Solstice displays, sacrifices, and funerals: they identified types and quantities and supplied them.
translations.idiomatic: For New Year's and Winter Solstice displays, sacrifices, and funerals, they identified each item by name and number and furnished them.

sentences.zh: 凡戎器，色別而異處，以衞尉幕士暴涼之。

translations.literal: In all, weapons were sorted by color and stored separately, and aired in the shade by curtain guardsmen of the Court of Palace Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons were sorted by color, stored apart, and aired in the shade by curtain guardsmen of the Court of Palace Revenues.

sentences.zh: 京衞旗畫蹲獸、立禽，行幸則給飛走旗。

translations.literal: Capital Guard flags were painted with crouching beasts and standing birds; on imperial progress, fly-and-walk flags were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Guard banners bore crouching beasts and standing birds; on imperial progress, fly-and-walk banners were issued.

sentences.zh: 凡諸衞儀仗，以御史涖其庋掌；

translations.literal: In all, ceremonial regalia of the various Guards was overseen by a censor who guarded the stores;
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial regalia of the various Guards was overseen by a censor who guarded the stores;

sentences.zh: 武庫器仗，則兵部長官涖其脩完。

translations.literal: weapons in the armory were overseen in their repair and upkeep by the Ministry of War minister.
translations.idiomatic: armory weapons were overseen in repair and upkeep by the Ministry of War minister.

sentences.zh: 京官五品以上征行者，假甲、纛、旗、幡、矟；

translations.literal: Capital officials of fifth rank and above on campaign were lent armor, battle standards, flags, pennants, and spears;
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of fifth rank and above setting out on campaign were lent armor, battle standards, flags, pennants, and spears;

sentences.zh: 諸衞，給弓；

translations.literal: the various Guards were issued bows;
translations.idiomatic: the various Guards received bows;

sentences.zh: 千牛，給甲。

translations.literal: Thousand-Ox Guard was issued armor.
translations.idiomatic: the Thousand-Ox Guard received armor.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Minister of Justice, one person, senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice had one minister of senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 侍郞一人，正四品下。

translations.literal: vice minister, one person, senior fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: one vice minister of senior fourth rank, lower grade.

sentences.zh: 掌律令、刑法、徒隸、按覆讞禁之政。

translations.literal: They managed the policies of statutes, penal law, convict laborers, and review and verification of cases and prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: They governed statutes, penal law, convict labor, and the review and verification of cases and prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰刑部，二曰都官，三曰比部，四曰司門。

translations.literal: Their subordinates were four: first Justice, second Convicts, third Audit, fourth Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus reported to them: Justice, Convicts, Audit, and Passes.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中、員外郎，掌律法，按覆大理及天下奏讞，為尚書、侍郎之貳。

translations.literal: Justice Bureau directors and vice directors managed penal law, reviewed and verified cases from the Court of Judicial Review and memorialized cases from throughout the realm, serving as deputies to the minister and vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Justice Bureau directors handled penal law, reviewed cases from the Court of Judicial Review and memorialized cases empire-wide, and served as deputies to the minister and vice minister.

sentences.zh: 凡刑法之書有四：一曰律，二曰令，三曰格，四曰式。

translations.literal: In all, there were four books of penal law: first Statutes, second Ordinances, third Rescripts, fourth Formularies.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law comprised four codes: Statutes, Ordinances, Rescripts, and Formularies.

sentences.zh: 凡鞫大獄，以尚書侍郎與御史中丞、大理卿為三司使。

translations.literal: In all, for trying major cases, the minister and vice minister joined the censor-in-chief and Court of Judicial Review director as Three Offices commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Major trials were heard by a commission of three: the minister and vice minister, the censor-in-chief, and the Court of Judicial Review director.

sentences.zh: 凡國有大赦，集囚徒于闕下以聽。

translations.literal: In all, when the state granted a general amnesty, convicts were assembled below the palace gate to hear it.
translations.idiomatic: On a general amnesty, convicts were gathered beneath the palace gate to hear the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事四人，都官主事二人，比部主事四人，司門主事二人。

translations.literal: Justice section chiefs four, Convicts section chiefs two, Audit section chiefs four, Passes section chiefs two.
translations.idiomatic: Justice had four section chiefs, Convicts two, Audit four, and Passes two.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，改刑部曰司刑，都官曰司僕，比部曰司計，司門曰司關。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, Justice was renamed Directorate of Punishment, Convicts renamed Directorate of Servants, Audit renamed Directorate of Accounts, Passes renamed Directorate of Barriers.
translations.idiomatic: In 662 Justice became the Directorate of Punishment, Convicts the Directorate of Servants, Audit the Directorate of Accounts, and Passes the Directorate of Barriers.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，改刑部曰秋官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, Justice was renamed Autumn Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 Justice was renamed the Autumn Office.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，改刑部曰司憲，比部曰司計。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, Justice was renamed Directorate of Law, Audit renamed Directorate of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 Justice became the Directorate of Law and Audit the Directorate of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 有刑部令史十九人，書令史三十八人，亭長六人，掌固十人；

translations.literal: There were nineteen Justice clerks, thirty-eight copy clerks, six station chiefs, and ten custodians;
translations.idiomatic: Justice employed nineteen clerks, thirty-eight copy clerks, six station chiefs, and ten custodians;

sentences.zh: 都官令史九人，書令史十二人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Convicts clerks nine, copy clerks twelve, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: Convicts nine clerks, twelve copy clerks, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 比部令史十四人，書令史二十七人，計史一人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Audit clerks fourteen, copy clerks twenty-seven, reckoning clerk one, custodians four;
translations.idiomatic: Audit fourteen clerks, twenty-seven copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 司門令史六人，書令史十三人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Passes clerks six, copy clerks thirteen, custodians four.
translations.idiomatic: Passes six clerks, thirteen copy clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 都官郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌俘隸簿錄，給衣糧醫藥，而理其訴免。

translations.literal: Convicts Bureau directors and vice directors, one each, managed registers of captives and convicts, supplied clothing, grain, and medicine, and adjudicated petitions for release.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts had one director and one vice director, who kept registers of captives and convicts, supplied clothing, grain, and medicine, and heard petitions for release.

sentences.zh: 凡反逆相坐，沒其家配官曹，長役為官奴婢。

translations.literal: In all, for treason and rebellion with guilt by association, the household was confiscated and assigned to government offices; adult males were long-term convict laborers serving as government slaves.
translations.idiomatic: In treason and rebellion with guilt by association, the household was confiscated and assigned to government offices, and adult males were long-term convict laborers—government slaves.

sentences.zh: 一免者，一歲三番役。

translations.literal: One exemption: three rotations of corvée per year.
translations.idiomatic: After one exemption, three corvée rotations per year.

sentences.zh: 再免為雜戶，亦曰官戶，二歲五番役。

translations.literal: Two exemptions made miscellaneous households, also called government households: five rotations of corvée every two years.
translations.idiomatic: After two exemptions they became miscellaneous households—also called government households—performing five corvée rotations every two years.

sentences.zh: 每番皆一月。

translations.literal: Each rotation was one month.
translations.idiomatic: Each rotation lasted one month.

sentences.zh: 三免為良人。

translations.literal: Three exemptions made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: After three exemptions they became commoners.

sentences.zh: 六十以上及廢疾者，為官戶；

translations.literal: Those sixty and above and the disabled became government households;
translations.idiomatic: Those sixty and above and the disabled were classed as government households;

sentences.zh: 七十為良人。

translations.literal: at seventy they became commoners.
translations.idiomatic: at seventy they became commoners.

sentences.zh: 每歲孟春上其籍，自黃口以上印臂，仲冬送於都官，條其生息而按比之。

translations.literal: Each year in early spring their registers were submitted upward; from children upward arms were stamped; in mid-winter they were sent to Convicts Bureau, which itemized births and growth and compared registers.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in early spring their registers went upward; from childhood upward arms were stamped; in mid-winter they were sent to the Convicts Bureau, which itemized births and growth and reconciled the rolls.

sentences.zh: 樂工、獸醫、騙馬、調馬、羣頭、栽接之人皆取焉。

translations.literal: Musicians, beast doctors, gelding masters, horse trainers, herd chiefs, and grafting specialists were all drawn from them.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians, veterinarians, gelding masters, horse trainers, herd chiefs, and grafting specialists were all recruited from their ranks.

sentences.zh: 附貫州縣者，按比如平民，不番上，歲督丁資，為錢一千五百；

translations.literal: Those attached to prefectures and counties were compared like commoners, did not report for rotation, and paid an annual adult-male levy of one thousand five hundred cash;
translations.idiomatic: Those registered in prefectures and counties were treated like commoners, exempt from rotation duty, and paid an annual adult-male levy of one thousand five hundred cash;

sentences.zh: 丁婢、中男，五輸其一；

translations.literal: for adult female slaves and middle youths, one in five paid;
translations.idiomatic: for adult female slaves and middle youths, one in five paid;

sentences.zh: 侍丁、殘疾半輸。

translations.literal: attending youths and the disabled paid half.
translations.idiomatic: attending youths and the disabled paid half.

sentences.zh: 凡居作者，差以三等：四歲以上，為小；

translations.literal: In all, for age categories of laborers, three grades were distinguished: four years and above were minors;
translations.idiomatic: Laborers fell into three age grades: four years and above counted as minors;

sentences.zh: 十一以上，為中；

translations.literal: eleven and above were middle youths;
translations.idiomatic: eleven and above as middle youths;

sentences.zh: 二十以上，為丁。

translations.literal: twenty and above were adult males.
translations.idiomatic: twenty and above as adult males.

sentences.zh: 丁奴，三當二役；

translations.literal: Adult male slaves counted as three for two rotations of corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Adult male slaves counted three for two corvée rotations;

sentences.zh: 中奴、丁婢，二當一役；

translations.literal: middle-youth slaves and adult female slaves counted as two for one rotation;
translations.idiomatic: middle-youth slaves and adult female slaves counted two for one rotation;

sentences.zh: 中婢，三當一役。

translations.literal: middle-youth female slaves counted as three for one rotation.
translations.idiomatic: middle-youth female slaves counted three for one rotation.

sentences.zh: 比部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌句會內外賦斂、經費、俸祿、公廨、勳賜、贓贖、徒役課程、逋欠之物，及軍資、械器、和糴、屯收所入。
