translations.literal: Audit Bureau directors and vice directors, one each, managed audit and reconciliation of internal and external tax levies, expenditures, salaries, government offices, merit grants, fines and ransoms, convict-labor quotas, and arrears, as well as military supplies, weapons, government grain purchases, and garrison harvest receipts.
translations.idiomatic: Audit had one director and one vice director, charged with reconciling internal and external tax levies, expenditures, salaries, government offices, merit grants, fines and ransoms, convict-labor quotas, and arrears, together with military supplies, weapons, government grain purchases, and garrison harvest receipts.

sentences.zh: 京師倉庫，三月一比，諸司、諸使、京都，四時句會於尚書省，以後季句前季；

translations.literal: Capital granaries and storehouses were audited every three months; the various offices, commissioners, and capital agencies quarterly reconciled accounts at the Department of State Affairs, each quarter auditing the previous quarter;
translations.idiomatic: Capital granaries and storehouses were audited every three months; every quarter the various offices, commissioners, and capital agencies reconciled accounts at the Department of State Affairs, each quarter closing the one before;

sentences.zh: 諸州，則歲終總句焉。

translations.literal: prefectures then made a year-end aggregate audit.
translations.idiomatic: prefectures submitted a year-end aggregate audit.

sentences.zh: 司門郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌門關出入之籍及闌遺之物。

translations.literal: Passes Bureau directors and vice directors, one each, managed registers of gate-pass entry and exit and lost-and-found articles.
translations.idiomatic: Passes had one director and one vice director, who kept gate-pass entry and exit registers and records of lost-and-found articles.

sentences.zh: 凡著籍，月一易之。

translations.literal: In all, registered persons had registers renewed monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Registered persons had their rolls renewed every month.

sentences.zh: 流內，記官爵、姓名；

translations.literal: Flow-within persons recorded office and rank, name;
translations.idiomatic: Flow-within persons were recorded by office, rank, and name;

sentences.zh: 流外，記年齒、貌狀。

translations.literal: flow-outside persons recorded age and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: flow-outside persons by age and appearance.

sentences.zh: 非遷解不除。

translations.literal: Entries were not removed unless upon transfer or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Entries were not struck unless upon transfer or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 凡有召者，降墨敕，勘銅魚、木契然後入。

translations.literal: In all, when someone was summoned, a black-ink edict was issued; bronze tally and wooden tally were verified, and only then entry was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone was summoned, a black-ink edict was issued; bronze tally and wooden tally were checked, and only then was entry allowed.

sentences.zh: 監門校尉巡日送平安。

translations.literal: Gate-Guard captains on patrol sent daily reports of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gate-Guard captains on patrol submitted daily reports that all was secure.

sentences.zh: 凡奏事，遣官送之，晝題時刻，夜題更籌。

translations.literal: In all, for memorials to the throne, officials were dispatched to deliver them; by day the hour was noted, by night the watch tally.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials to the throne were delivered by dispatched officials; by day the hour was marked, by night the watch tally.

sentences.zh: 命婦諸親朝參者，內侍監校尉涖索。

translations.literal: Titled ladies and imperial relatives attending court had their persons searched under supervision by Inner Service Bureau captains.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies and imperial relatives attending court were searched under supervision by Inner Service Bureau captains.

sentences.zh: 凡葦軬車，不入宮門。

translations.literal: In all, reed-canopied carts did not enter the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Reed-canopied carts were not permitted through the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 闌遺之物，揭於門外，牓以物色，期年沒官。

translations.literal: Lost-and-found objects were posted outside the gate, placarded with descriptions of their appearance; after one full year they were forfeited to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Unclaimed goods were displayed outside the gate with placards describing their appearance; after a year they escheated to the state.

sentences.zh: 天下關二十六，有上、中、下之差，度者，本司給過所；

translations.literal: There were twenty-six passes throughout the realm, with distinctions of upper, middle, and lower grade; travelers received travel permits from their own agency;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six passes spanned the empire, graded upper, middle, and lower; travelers received transit permits from their home office;

sentences.zh: 出塞踰月者，給行牒；

translations.literal: those crossing the frontier for more than a month received travel documents;
translations.idiomatic: those leaving the frontier for longer than a month received frontier travel documents;

sentences.zh: 獵手所過，給長籍，三月一易。

translations.literal: hunting parties passing through received long registers, renewed every three months.
translations.idiomatic: hunting parties in transit received long-term registers, exchanged every three months.

sentences.zh: 蕃客往來，閱其裝重，入一關者，餘關不譏。

translations.literal: When foreign envoys and merchants traveled, their baggage weight was inspected; once they had entered one pass, the remaining passes did not scrutinize them again.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests were weighed at the first pass they entered; thereafter the other passes did not re-inspect their baggage.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書一人，正三品；

translations.literal: Minister of Works, one person, senior third rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works had one minister of senior third rank;

sentences.zh: 侍郞一人，正四品下。

translations.literal: vice minister, one person, senior fourth rank, lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: one vice minister of junior fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 掌山澤、屯田、工匠、諸司公廨紙墨之事。

translations.literal: They managed mountains and marshes, garrison fields, artisans, and the paper and ink supplies of all agency offices.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw mountains and marshes, garrison agriculture, artisans, and the paper and ink for every government office.

sentences.zh: 其屬有四：一曰工部，二曰屯田，三曰虞部，四曰水部。

translations.literal: Their subordinates were four: first Works, second Garrison Fields, third Parklands, fourth Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Four bureaus reported to it: Works, Garrison Fields, Parklands, and Waterways.

sentences.zh: 工部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌城池土木之工役程式，為尚書、侍郎之貳。

translations.literal: Director and vice director of the Works Bureau, one each, managed regulations for city walls and civil construction labor, serving as deputies to the minister and vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Bureau had one director and one vice director, who set standards for fortifications and public works and served as the minister's deputies.

sentences.zh: 凡京都營繕，皆下少府、將作共其用，役千功者先奏。

translations.literal: All capital construction projects were assigned to the Court of the Imperial Treasures and the Directorate of Palace Buildings to share materials; projects requiring a thousand work-units required prior memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Capital repairs were routed through the Court of the Imperial Treasures and the Directorate of Palace Buildings for shared supplies; any project of a thousand work-units had to be memorialized in advance.

sentences.zh: 凡工匠，以州縣為團，五人為火，五火置長一人。

translations.literal: Artisans were organized by prefecture and county into squads; five men formed a fire unit, and every five fire units had one chief.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans were mustered by prefecture and county into teams of five called fire units; every five fire units had one foreman.

sentences.zh: 四月至七月為長功，二月、三月、八月、九月為中功，十月至正月為短功。

translations.literal: April through July counted as long-work seasons; February, March, August, and September as medium-work; October through January as short-work.
translations.idiomatic: April to July was the long-work season, February–March and August–September the medium-work season, and October to January the short-work season.

sentences.zh: 雇者，日為絹三尺，內中尚巧匠，無作則納資。

translations.literal: Hired laborers received three feet of silk per day; skilled artisans attached to the Inner Palace who had no work paid a fee instead.
translations.idiomatic: Day laborers were paid three feet of silk per day; master craftsmen on the palace rolls who had no assignment paid a substitute levy.

sentences.zh: 凡津梁道路，治以九月。

translations.literal: Ferries, bridges, and roads were maintained in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Ferries, bridges, and highways were repaired in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 工部主事三人，屯田主事二人，虞部主事二人，水部主事二人。

translations.literal: Works Bureau section chiefs three, Garrison Fields section chiefs two, Parklands section chiefs two, Waterways section chiefs two.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Bureau had three section chiefs, Garrison Fields two, Parklands two, and Waterways two.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，改起部曰工部，龍朔二年，曰司平，屯田曰司田，虞部曰司虞，水部曰司川。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude the Directorate of Construction was renamed Ministry of Works; in the second year of Longshuo it became Directorate of Equilibrium, Garrison Fields became Bureau of Fields, Parklands became Bureau of Parks, and Waterways became Bureau of Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 the Directorate of Construction became the Ministry of Works; in 662 the ministry became the Directorate of Equilibrium, Garrison Fields the Bureau of Fields, Parklands the Bureau of Parks, and Waterways the Bureau of Rivers.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，改工部曰冬官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai the Ministry of Works was renamed the Directorate of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 it was renamed the Directorate of Winter.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，改虞部曰司虞，水部曰司水。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao Parklands was renamed Bureau of Parks and Waterways was renamed Bureau of Waters.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 Parklands became the Bureau of Parks and Waterways the Bureau of Waters.

sentences.zh: 工部有令史十二人，書令史二十一人，計史一人，亭長六人，掌固八人；

translations.literal: The Works Bureau had twelve clerks, twenty-one copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, six station chiefs, and eight custodians;
translations.idiomatic: The Works Bureau employed twelve clerks, twenty-one copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, six station chiefs, and eight custodians;

sentences.zh: 屯田令史七人，書令史十二人，計史一人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Garrison Fields seven clerks, twelve copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, four custodians;
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Fields seven clerks, twelve copy clerks, one reckoning clerk, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 虞部令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人；

translations.literal: Parklands four clerks, nine copy clerks, four custodians;
translations.idiomatic: Parklands four clerks, nine copy clerks, and four custodians;

sentences.zh: 水部令史四人，書令史九人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: Waterways four clerks, nine copy clerks, four custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Waterways four clerks, nine copy clerks, and four custodians.

sentences.zh: 屯田郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌天下屯田及京文武職田、諸司公廨田，以品給焉。

translations.literal: Director and vice director of Garrison Fields, one each, managed garrison agriculture throughout the realm, official salary fields for capital civil and military officials, and agency office lands, allotting them by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Fields had one director and one vice director, who administered state farming colonies empire-wide, salary lands for capital officials civil and military, and office plots for government agencies, apportioned by rank.

sentences.zh: 虞部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌京都衢閧、苑囿、山澤草木及百官蕃客時蔬薪炭供頓、畋獵之事。

translations.literal: Director and vice director of Parklands, one each, managed capital streets and alleys, imperial parks, mountains and marshes with their vegetation, seasonal vegetables and firewood and charcoal for officials and foreign guests at waystations, and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Parklands had one director and one vice director, who oversaw the capital's streets and parks, mountain and marsh lands and their flora, provisions of fresh produce, fuel, and waystation supplies for officials and foreign guests, and the hunting grounds.

sentences.zh: 每歲春，以戶小兒、戶婢仗內蒔種溉灌，冬則謹其蒙覆。

translations.literal: Each spring household boys and maids were assigned within the parks to sow, plant, and irrigate; in winter they carefully maintained protective coverings.
translations.idiomatic: Every spring, boys and maids from registered households were detailed inside the parks to plant and water; in winter they tended the protective mulching.

sentences.zh: 凡郊祠神壇、五岳名山，樵採、芻牧皆有禁，距壝三十步外得耕種，春夏不伐木。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrificial altars and the famous mountains of the Five Peaks, fuel-gathering and pasturing were forbidden; cultivation was permitted beyond thirty paces from the enclosing mound; trees were not felled in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Around suburban altars and the Five Sacred Peaks, woodcutting and grazing were prohibited; farming was allowed only beyond thirty paces from the ritual enclosure, and felling trees was banned in spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南府三百里內，正月、五月、九月禁弋獵。

translations.literal: Within three hundred li of the Jingzhao and Henan prefectures, hunting with bow and net was forbidden in the first, fifth, and ninth months.
translations.idiomatic: Within three hundred li of the Jingzhao and Henan metropolitan prefectures, fowling and hunting were forbidden in the first, fifth, and ninth months.

sentences.zh: 山澤有寶可供用者，以聞。

translations.literal: When mountains or marshes yielded treasures fit for use, report was made to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When useful treasures were found in mountains or marshes, the discovery was reported upward.

sentences.zh: 水部郎中、員外郎，各一人，掌津濟、船艫、渠梁、堤堰、溝洫、漁捕、運漕、碾磑之事。

translations.literal: Director and vice director of Waterways, one each, managed ferries, shipping, canals and bridges, dikes and dams, drainage ditches, fishing, grain transport, and water-powered mills.
translations.idiomatic: Waterways had one director and one vice director, who handled ferries, shipping, canals and bridges, dikes and sluices, irrigation ditches, fisheries, grain transport, and water mills.

sentences.zh: 凡坑陷、井穴皆有標。

translations.literal: All pits, sinkholes, and wells were marked.
translations.idiomatic: Every pit, sinkhole, and well had to be posted with warning markers.

sentences.zh: 京畿有渠長、斗門長。

translations.literal: In the capital region there were canal chiefs and sluice-gate chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The capital districts had canal overseers and sluice-gate overseers.

sentences.zh: 諸州堤堰，刺史、縣令以時檢行，而涖其決築。

translations.literal: In the various prefectures, prefects and magistrates inspected dikes and dams on schedule and supervised breaches and repairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, prefects and magistrates inspected dikes and dams at the proper season and directed emergency repairs.

sentences.zh: 有埭，則以下戶分牽，禁爭利者。

translations.literal: Where there were earthen dams for boat haulage, lower-grade households were assigned in rotation to haul boats; profiteering was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Where haulage dams existed, lower-status households were rotated to tow boats through them, and private profit-seeking was prohibited.
